title: Identifying the Components of AI Algorithm-Based Interactive Industrial Design
abstract: This study aimed to identify and explain the components of AI algorithm-based interactive industrial design and to develop a conceptual framework for organizing its contextual conditions, inputs, processes, and outputs. This applied qualitative study was conducted using a meta-synthesis approach. The research corpus included national and international studies related to interactive industrial design, artificial intelligence, generative design, human–machine interaction, human–robot interaction, industrial knowledge management, and intelligent technologies published between 2020 and 2026. Data were collected through a systematic search of reputable scientific databases. After removing duplicate, irrelevant, and methodologically weak sources, 55 studies were selected for final analysis. The seven-step model proposed by Sandelowski and Barroso was used to conduct the meta-synthesis. The quality of the selected studies was assessed using the Critical Appraisal Skills Programme checklist, and coding reliability was examined through inter-coder agreement. The meta-synthesis findings indicated that the components of AI algorithm-based interactive industrial design can be classified into 4 main categories, 19 concepts, and 96 codes. The main categories were context, inputs, process, and outputs. At the contextual level, digital transformation, technological and data-driven infrastructure, human–machine interaction, ethical requirements, trust, and knowledge management were identified. The input category included user data, interactive needs, design and environmental data, AI algorithms and technologies, and human expertise. The process category comprised design problem identification, data collection and preparation, intelligent analysis, generation of design alternatives, human–AI interaction in the design loop, simulation, evaluation, optimization, and continuous learning. The output category included improved design quality and accuracy, innovation and creativity, enhanced user experience, increased productivity, strengthened design decision-making, knowledge management, and ethical, organizational, and social implications. AI-based interactive industrial design is a multidimensional, data-driven, human-centered, and learning-oriented approach that integrates algorithmic analytical capabilities with human creativity and expertise to enhance the quality, innovation, interactivity, and effectiveness of industrial design processes.

title: Designing a Business Intelligence Model for Enhancing Brand Performance in the Food Industry of Tehran Province: A Grounded Theory Approach
abstract: This study aimed to design and explain a context-specific business intelligence model for enhancing the brand performance of companies operating in the food industry of Tehran Province. This applied and exploratory qualitative study was conducted using the grounded theory methodology. The research population comprised senior managers and experts working in the food industry of Tehran Province, who were selected through purposive and judgmental sampling. Data were collected through in-depth, directed interviews with 12 participants who possessed relevant managerial experience and expertise in marketing, commercial planning, and the food industry. The data were analyzed according to the systematic approach of Strauss and Corbin through open, axial, and selective coding. Participant feedback and peer review were employed to establish the credibility of the findings. Recoding was also performed to assess reliability, producing an intercoder test–retest reliability coefficient of 0.83. The findings indicated that market competition, emerging technologies, organizational needs, and data quality constituted the causal conditions underlying the development of business intelligence. The central phenomenon was the analysis of data to generate valuable information, encompassing data collection, storage, analysis, application, and the monitoring of key performance indicators. Technological infrastructure, organizational structure, top management support, and regulatory requirements were identified as contextual conditions facilitating model implementation. Environmental turbulence, economic conditions, resistance to change, and government interventions functioned as intervening conditions. The principal strategies included data-driven analysis and decision-making, value creation and competitive advantage, organizational flexibility and responsiveness, intelligent supply-chain and production management, brand-value enhancement, and improved marketing communications. These strategies resulted in more accurate market and customer analysis, strategic brand decision-making, organizational innovation, greater brand value and differentiation, and enhanced brand sustainability and customer trust. Business intelligence represents a strategic and dynamic organizational capability through which market and organizational data are transformed into actionable knowledge. Its effective implementation can strengthen evidence-based decision-making, organizational adaptability, customer trust, brand differentiation, and sustainable competitive advantage in the food industry.

title: Design and Validation of a Comprehensive Digital Banking Performance Evaluation Model Using a Stakeholder Approach: A Case Study of Bank Saderat Iran
abstract: This study aimed to design and validate a comprehensive stakeholder-oriented model for evaluating digital banking performance in Bank Saderat Iran. This applied mixed-method study was conducted in three sequential phases. In the qualitative phase, semi-structured interviews were conducted with 30 digital banking experts and stakeholders, including managers, employees, customers, and shareholders of Bank Saderat Iran in Tehran. Participants were selected through purposive and snowball sampling until theoretical saturation was reached. The data were analyzed using thematic analysis in MAXQDA. Content validity was assessed through the Content Validity Ratio and Content Validity Index, while coding reliability was evaluated using Holsti’s coefficient. In the quantitative phase, a researcher-developed questionnaire based on the qualitative findings was administered to 250 participants. Data were analyzed using SPSS 23 and SmartPLS 3 through partial least squares structural equation modeling. Qualitative analysis identified 14 global themes constituting the principal dimensions of the model. All factor loadings exceeded 0.50 and were statistically significant. Cronbach’s alpha coefficients ranged from 0.799 to 0.940, Rho_A values from 0.804 to 0.951, composite reliability values from 0.868 to 0.957, and AVE values from 0.623 to 0.848. All structural paths were statistically significant. Digital trust and security showed the strongest path coefficient (β = 0.880), followed by competitive sustainability of digital banking (β = 0.384) and technical and infrastructural performance (β = 0.198). The coefficient of determination was R² = 0.906, indicating very high explanatory power of the proposed model. The validated model demonstrated that digital banking performance should be evaluated beyond financial and technological indicators by simultaneously incorporating customer-related, human resource, governance, security, competitive, stakeholder-value, participatory, and environmental dimensions. The proposed framework can therefore provide a comprehensive basis for assessing and strategically managing digital transformation in Bank Saderat Iran.

title: Designing a Model to Explain the Role of Social Media and Influencers in Customer Relationship Management and Branding in the Beauty Industry
abstract: This study aimed to design and validate a model explaining the role of social media and influencers in customer relationship management and branding in the beauty industry. This applied study employed an exploratory mixed-methods design incorporating qualitative and quantitative phases. In the qualitative phase, thematic analysis was conducted following Braun and Clarke’s six-stage approach. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews with 12 theoretical and practical experts in business management, marketing, customer relationship management, and social media, selected through purposive sampling and theoretical judgment. The qualitative analysis identified seven major themes: trust and credibility, influencer role and performance, brand strategy for influencer management, customer relationship management, customer loyalty, branding and brand identity, and innovative strategies. In the quantitative phase, the statistical population consisted of marketing experts, specialists, and managers working in the beauty industry, and 384 participants were included. Data were collected using a questionnaire and analyzed through partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). Convergent and discriminant validity, composite reliability, and Cronbach’s alpha were also assessed and confirmed. Inferential results indicated that all seven structural paths were positive and statistically significant (t>2.58, p<0.01). Customer relationship management demonstrated the strongest effect on customer relationship management and branding (β=0.553), followed by customer loyalty (β=0.542), trust and credibility (β=0.422), influencer role and performance (β=0.369), innovative strategies (β=0.362), brand strategy for influencer management (β=0.308), and branding and brand identity (β=0.267). The model explained 62.1% of the variance in the dependent construct (R²=0.621). The predictive relevance index was Q²=0.390, while the overall goodness-of-fit index was 0.655, indicating strong explanatory and predictive performance. The findings indicate that the effectiveness of social media and influencers in the beauty industry depends on the integrated contribution of relationship-oriented, trust-based, loyalty-building, branding, and innovative mechanisms. Customer relationship management, customer loyalty, and trust and credibility emerged as the most influential dimensions. Accordingly, beauty brands can strengthen their market position by integrating customer relationship management with influencer marketing strategies and developing personalized, credible, and interactive relationships with consumers.

title: Designing a Model for Customer Behavior Analysis in Banking Using Artificial Intelligence
abstract: This study aimed to develop and validate a model for analyzing and predicting bank customers’ behavior using artificial intelligence. This research was basic-applied in terms of purpose, sequential exploratory mixed-methods in terms of data type, cross-sectional in terms of data collection time, and based on content analysis and meta-synthesis in the qualitative phase and descriptive-survey procedures in the quantitative phase. In the qualitative phase, the statistical population included all studies related to customer behavior in banking systems and the factors and indicators affecting its analysis and prediction, published in valid databases between 2000 and 2025. After screening through the PRISMA procedure, 84 studies were selected for final analysis. Extracted concepts were classified into components and broader dimensions. In the quantitative phase, combined data from banking customers, along with the views of banking experts and customer-relationship specialists, were used. A researcher-made questionnaire derived from the qualitative phase was applied to assess the model components. Customer behavior prediction was performed using decision tree, support vector machine, and deep learning based on Transformer architecture. The qualitative findings led to the identification of 49 concepts, 22 components, and 12 main dimensions. The identified components included individual characteristics, financial status, responsiveness, reliability, assurance, digital experience, in-person experience, transparency, security, service satisfaction, value satisfaction, offer characteristics, communications, campaign response, brand value, transaction patterns, consumption patterns, channel preference, cooperation continuity, brand advocacy, reduced use, and offer acceptance. In the quantitative phase, the decision tree model showed the strongest predictive performance, with an R² of 0.8327, MAE of 0.0421, and RMSE of 0.0532. The support vector machine model ranked second, followed by the deep learning model, although all three algorithms demonstrated acceptable predictive capability. The proposed model demonstrated that integrating demographic, financial, behavioral, experiential, transactional, and marketing-related data can provide a valid basis for analyzing and predicting bank customers’ behavior. The findings indicate that artificial intelligence algorithms, particularly decision trees, can support banks in identifying hidden behavioral patterns, personalizing services, reducing customer churn, improving campaign effectiveness, and strengthening managerial decision-making in customer relationship management.

title: Supplementary Material for "Same Same, but Different: How Dedicated AI Leadership Roles Differentiate from Technology Leadership"
abstract: Supplementary material for the article: Markic, M., Hennemann, S. & Poeppelbuss, J. (2027). Same Same, but Different: How Dedicated AI Leadership Roles Differentiate from Technology Leadership. Hawaii International Conference on System Sciences (HICSS) 2027. Abstract: Organizations across industries increasingly create dedicated artificial intelligence (AI) leadership roles alongside, rather than in place of, established technology leadership roles, although the literature suggests that governance demands could be absorbed by existing leadership roles. In this study, we examine how new AI leadership roles are defined and how they differ from established leadership roles. Adopting a governance-demands-and-skills lens, we conduct a large-language-model-assisted content analysis of 794 job ads. Our findings reveal that AI leadership roles entail a distinctive governance mandate – coordinating AI across business units, aligning it with strategic value, translating between technical and business domains, building governance mechanisms, and managing enablement – which existing technology leadership roles encode only partially. Therefore, we argue that AI leadership roles are configured as organizational responses to a residual governance gap that existing leadership roles leave unaddressed.

title: PREPARATION, SPECTRAL CHARACTERIZATION, MOLECULAR DOCKING, ANDANTIOXIDANT ACTIVITY OF NEW SYMMETRICAL DIMERS DERIVATIVES OFOXAZEPINE STARTING FROM PYRIDINE-5,7-DIONE ANHYDRIDE
abstract: This study reports the synthesis of a series of oxazepine derivatives via a condensation reaction between amines and various benzaldehyde derivatives, using benzene as the solvent. The resulting intermediates were subsequently reacted with pyridine-5,7-dione anhydride in dry benzene to afford oxazepine derivatives (H1–H6). The synthesized compounds were characterized by Fourier-transform infrared (FT-IR) spectroscopy, proton nuclear magnetic resonance (¹H-NMR) spectroscopy, and mass spectrometry. Reaction progress was monitored using thin-layer chromatography (TLC). The antioxidant activity of compounds H1–H6 was evaluated and compared with that of vitamin C. In addition, molecular docking studies were performed for selected compounds (H1, H4, and H6) against tyrosinase (PDB ID: 3NM8) to identify optimal binding sites and evaluate interactions with neighboring residues. The docked complexes exhibited RMSD values of 1.16, 1.40, and 1.30 Å for H1, H4, and H6, respectively. Among the tested compounds, H4 showed the highest binding affinity, in good agreement with the experimental results. Overall, the synthesized oxazepine derivatives demonstrated moderate antioxidant activity, warranting further in vivo investigation.

title: AI-Powered Cyberbullying Detection and Prevention for Safer Digital Spaces
abstract: This research aims to address the growing issue of cyberbullying, particularly among youth, by developing an AI-powered system for real-time detection and prevention on digital platforms. The research focuses on understanding the various forms of cyberbullying and their detrimental effects on mental health. Using the Agile system development methodology, the research will follow an iterative process involving design, development, and testing phases to create a reliable detection tool. The system is intended to identify harmful online behaviour and alert parents or guardians promptly. Preliminary results suggest that the tool will feature an intuitive user interface and effective algorithms capable of detecting abusive interactions. This research is significant, as it proposes a technological solution to a pressing social issue, aiming to enhance the safety and well-being of young people online. Additionally, the research aligns with SDG 16 Peace, Justice, and Strong Institutions by contributing to the protection of children from online harm and promoting safer, more just digital environments.

title: Advancements and Optimization Strategies for Hybrid Photovoltaic–Diesel–Battery Systems in Remote and Off-Grid Applications: A Narrative Review
abstract: Hybrid photovoltaic (PV)–diesel–battery systems are an important option for remote and off-grid electrification, where diesel generation remains common despite high fuel costs, emissions, and logistical constraints. This structured narrative review synthesizes developments in system architecture, DC–DC converter topology, energy management, communication, and techno-economic optimization. The reviewed evidence indicates that integrating PV generation and battery storage can reduce diesel operation, improve autonomy, and lower lifecycle costs when components and dispatch strategies are matched to local conditions. In one representative study, total modeled pollutant emissions decreased from 15,922 kg/year for a diesel-only system to 606.9 kg/year for a PV–diesel–battery system, a reduction of approximately 96%. Remaining barriers include capital cost, battery degradation, application-layer interoperability, cybersecurity, and limited field validation of advanced artificial-intelligence-based control. The synthesis also shows that published cost of energy, net present cost, and renewable-fraction values should not be compared without accounting for location, load, fuel price, component cost, discount rate, and reliability assumptions.

title: A stratified ecological model of injury etiology in professional football: a context‑driven “game model” of injury risk constraints management and foresight reasoning under uncertainty
abstract: Understanding sports injury etiology, causation, and risk mitigation remains a central focus in sports medicine research.However, current models remain generic, neglecting the sport-specific characteristics and environmental specificities that shape both injury-risk and -resilience.This gap is especially critical in football, where injury risk is inherently intricate and multifactorial.To address this, we propose a novel conceptual approach built around a context-driven "Game Model", specifically tailored to the football's complexity.The core of our model is centred on the principle that a player's injury-risk is directly dependent on the dynamics and context of the team/club rather than being solely determined by a simple causality of prematurely and haphazardly musculoskeletal "intrinsic factors".Our model is structured around five superposed "Ecological Strata", which incorporate the concept of "contextual drivers" mapping the non-linear dynamics of the different constraints within the football environment that influence team and player injury-risk.Through this structure, we bring to light overlooked elements, including player interconnection, non-exposure, response versus adaptation, delayed recursive loop, non-time-loss injuries and foresight-driven clinical reasoning paired with hindsight clinical review, each capturing a dimension of risk that linear models fail to account for.Taken together, our context-driven approach reframes injury-risk recognition as dynamic, contextual, and intuitive, allowing clinicians to navigate, rather than merely react to uncertainty.In doing so, our model offers operational perspectives and windows of opportunities for injury-risk constraints management, enabling more proactive clinical reasoning and transdisciplinary collaborative decision-making, alongside targeted interventions to maintain and develop player health, robustness and performance within the football environment.

title: Identifying the Factors Affecting the Feasibility of Lean Production toward Sustainability in the Iranian Automotive Industry Using Grey Theory
abstract: This study aimed to identify and prioritize the factors affecting the feasibility of transitioning from lean production toward sustainability in the Iranian automotive industry using qualitative thematic analysis and Grey Relational Analysis. This applied study employed an exploratory sequential mixed-methods design. In the qualitative phase, data were collected through a review of the literature and semi-structured interviews with 18 academic and professional experts selected purposively, with interviews continuing until theoretical saturation. The qualitative data were analyzed through open, axial, and selective coding to identify the principal dimensions and factors influencing sustainable lean production. In the quantitative phase, a researcher-developed questionnaire based on the extracted qualitative codes was administered to a population of 400 healthcare personnel in Ilam to assess the generalizability of the organizational components in a high-pressure service environment. Content and construct validity and Cronbach's alpha reliability were evaluated. Grey Relational Analysis was then used to transform uncertain judgments into grey numbers, normalize the data, calculate grey relational coefficients, and rank the identified factors. The analysis identified four overarching dimensions: technical and operational, economic and financial, environmental, and organizational and cultural. Grey Relational Analysis ranked reduction of production errors as the most influential factor (0.945), followed by process quality control (0.938), process optimization (0.931), reduction of production cycle time (0.924), and increased equipment efficiency (0.917). Waste reduction also received a high priority (0.910). Among supply-chain and technology factors, sustainable supply of raw materials ranked highest (0.840), while reduction of energy consumption was the leading environmental factor (0.735). Senior management support was the highest-ranked managerial factor (0.630). The transition toward sustainable lean production in the Iranian automotive industry should begin with operational stabilization and quality improvement, followed by supply-chain integration, digitalization, environmental efficiency, and sustained managerial and organizational support.

title: Savouring Peru through tourists’ profiles. An artificial neural networks perspective
abstract: This study aims to determine the variations occurring across different constructs concerning the importance of gastronomy — motivation to travel, willingness to visit specific destinations, gastronomic aspects and experiences, and emotions — in accordance with tourists’ sociodemographic profiles (age, gender, university education, and income). Based on 1,042 valid questionnaires, an artificial neural network (ANN) was developed using sociodemographic profile characteristics as input variables. This approach is useful for developing products and services tailored to tourists interested in gastronomy. The results indicate that age is the most influential variable in the model, with younger tourists attributing higher values to the constructs examined. These findings contribute to the body of research on gastronomic tourism in Peru and offer practical guidance for market segmentation and the management of tourist destinations.

title: From Symptoms to Diagnosis: Interpretation of Patient-Reported Orofacial Pain in Temporomandibular Disorders Among Dentists: A Cross-Sectional Study
abstract: Objectives: This study aimed to explore how dentists interpret patient-reported orofacial pain in TMDs and to identify key factors influencing diagnostic accuracy and clinical decision-making. Materials and Methods:A cross-sectional, scenario-based survey was conducted among 466 practicing dentists.The instrument incorporated clinically relevant patient-reported symptom scenarios to evaluate diagnostic interpretation, alongside measures of professional background, diagnostic confidence, and use of standardized criteria.Statistical analysis included descriptive methods, Chi-square testing, and multivariate logistic regression to identify independent predictors of diagnostic accuracy.Results: Marked variability was observed in the interpretation of patient-reported symptoms, particularly in ambiguous and non-specific presentations.Higher diagnostic accuracy was significantly associated with formal TMD training, greater clinical experience, and increased diagnostic confidence (p < 0.05).Dentists employing an integrative diagnostic approach-combining patient-reported symptoms with clinical examination-demonstrated superior performance (p < 0.01).Furthermore, consistent application of standardized diagnostic frameworks was strongly linked to improved interpretative accuracy (p < 0.001).Conclusions: These findings highlight substantial heterogeneity in dentists' interpretation of patient-reported orofacial pain, underscoring the complexity of diagnostic decisionmaking in TMDs.Enhancing clinician training and reinforcing the use of structured diagnostic criteria are essential to improve diagnostic consistency, accuracy, and patient outcomes.

title: A Hybrid Eulerian-Lagrangian Probability Model for Predicting Paraffin Deposits in Ball Valves During High-Paraffin Oil Transportation
abstract: This paper develops a hybrid Eulerian-Lagrangian probabilistic model for predicting asphaltene-resin-paraffin deposit (ARPD) formation in ball valves. A new approach to describing the deposition process is proposed, in which the carrier phase ( highly paraffin oil) is specified by an analytical velocity field, and the dispersed phase is modeled by an ensemble of particles. The key element of the study is the probabilistic function of particle adhesion to the wall, which takes into account three factors: oil supercooling relative to the wax onset temperature (WAT), the distance to the wall, and the local flow velocity. A particle recirculation algorithm is implemented, ensuring the preservation of the total particle number and the statistical significance of the ensemble throughout the simulation. A series of computational experiments showed that the model correctly reproduces the threshold nature of paraffin deposits (deposition begins only at T < WAT ) and allows observing the three-phase dynamics of the narrowing of the flow area. The model revealed that the most intense fouling occurs not in the narrowest cross-section of the ball valve, but in the adjacent transition zones ("seats"), which is explained by hydrodynamic conditions. The model was verified, confirming that the boundary conditions for no-flow are met and particles remain in the system.

title: CFD Investigation of Thermal and Electrical Behavior of Photovoltaic Modules Equipped with Heat Sinks and Vortex Generators
abstract: The Photovoltaic (PV) modules suffer performance losses at high operating temperatures, especially in hot and low-wind conditions, making effective cooling essential. This study numerically investigates a fan-assisted PV cooling duct equipped with heat sinks and vortex generators (VGs) using computational fluid dynamics (CFD). The novelty of the work lies in the integrated evaluation of duct height, fin spacing, VG height, inclination angle, and attack angle within a single forced-convection framework. The model was validated against published benchmark data with deviations below 5%. The results demonstrate that the reduction of duct height from 200 mm to 100 mm can decrease the PV surface temperature by 10 °C and among all finned cases, the array with 22 fins exhibited maximum cooling whilst the best compromise between heat-transfer enhancement and pressure drop was provided by using an arrangement with 18 fins in a given area. Thermal performance improved with increasing VG height, but the 40 mm VG gave the greatest heat-transfer coefficient at the cost of relatively high-pressure loss. In the 90° case, VG orientation achieved the highest electrical efficiency at (Re = 11000), achieving an electrical efficiency of 16.9% and maximum achievable electrical power output of approximately 44.21 W, after accounting for DC fan power consumption, with the 90° VG configuration still showing the highest system electrical power. The 30° scenario, by contrast, resulted in the best thermal efficiency–nearly 80% and the greatest thermal power–over 420 W demonstrating practical merit in providing guidance for selecting PV cooling configurations based on specific electrical-output or thermal-recovery priorities.

title: A Comprehensive Methodology for the Integrated Assessment of Road Safety of Transport and Technological Vehicles Based on Fuzzy Logic
abstract: In conditions of increasing complexity and intensity of transportation systems, ensuring road safety requires a transition to proactive and predictive methods of integral risk management. In this work a hierarchical model based on fuzzy logic has been developed to assess the safety of vehicle fleets by aggregating heterogeneous real-time data. To implement a comprehensive assessment, an algorithm has been proposed that performs automated multi-criteria analysis by merging key safety indicators related to technical condition, driver behavior, and operational factors. This algorithm calculates an integrated safety assessment, ranks carriers by risk level, and identifies potential violations. A method of adaptive membership functions has been applied to handle uncertainty and qualitative parameters. A verification study was conducted on theoretical cases covering a range of operational scenarios. A software solution — a Python module for fuzzy inference and visualization has also been implemented, expanding the capabilities of intelligent transportation systems. The results demonstrate that the developed system correctly ranks transport enterprises by risk level. Verification on five theoretical cases (TK1-TK5) confirmed the model's ability to generate an Integrated Safety Assessment (ISA) from 0 to 1, effectively distinguishing between exemplary compliance and systematic critical violations. For instance, a critically problematic scenario (TK4) received a low ISA of 0.34, signaling the need for immediate intervention, while a case with systematic violations (TK5) scored 0.55, near the predefined acceptability threshold of 0.5.

title: Dual-Objective Design of Broadband Rectenna and Anchor Node Optimization for Energy Harvesting and High-Accuracy UWB Localization
abstract: Wireless sensor networks and portable devices face two major challenges: sustainable energy supply and high-precision indoor localization. While far-field wireless power transfer (WPT) offers energy solutions, it suffers from low power density and environmental sensitivity. To mitigate these drawbacks, the proposed system incorporates polarization diversity and a wideband impedance matching strategy. Simultaneously, GPS fails in indoor environments, driving the need for ultra-wideband (UWB) localization to achieve centimeter-level accuracy. This paper presents a dual-objective framework to tackle both issues. First, it designs a broadband antenna array (1–20 GHz) with multi-polarization reception, combined with an optimized matching network and Schottky-based rectifier to enhance RF-to-DC conversion under low power. Second, it introduces an anchor placement optimization algorithm for UWB that uses probabilistic target behavior models to minimize positioning errors. Simulation results confirm that the energy harvester remains effective across various incident angles and frequencies, while the localization error is consistently reduced to around one centimeter. The integrated approach provides a comprehensive solution for next-generation WSNs, overcoming power management bottlenecks while elevating localization accuracy to approximately one centimeter.

title: Testing of Multi-Section Deep Well Sampler and Fluid Sampling from Borehole 5G at Vostok Station, Antarctica
abstract: Testing of the Multi-section Deep Well Sampler (MDWS) was conducted during the 70th Russian Antarctic Expedition at Vostok Station in 2024/25. The MDWS is a non-circulating piston sampler designed to collect borehole fluid samples from multiple depths in a single round trip. Surface tests verified the operational integrity of the electromechanical system and identified optimal performance parameters. The MDWS was then tested in Borehole 5G-5 at depths from 1,250 m to 3,597.4 m across six round trips, collecting 18 samples under extreme conditions (temperatures down to –60°C and pressures up to 350 atm). The device successfully passed all tests, proving its efficiency for Arctic and Antarctic applications and confirming its manufacturability at the Empress Catherine II Saint Petersburg Mining University, Russian Federation.

title: Programming-Based Computational Modelling for Freight Distribution Using Clarke–Wright Savings Method for Route Optimization: A Case Study in Surabaya, Indonesia
abstract: Urban freight pickup in dense metropolitan areas is constrained by short service windows, congestion, and limited vehicle capacity. This study evaluates a practical hybrid heuristic—Clarke-Wright Savings for clustering and Nearest Neighbor for sequencing—for evening pickup operations at a major Indonesian postal logistics hub in Surabaya. Using 46 pickup locations, the MATLAB implementation assesses service coverage, route-time feasibility, fleet requirement, distance efficiency, and capacity utilization under a 500-unit vehicle capacity and a 150-minute maximum route duration. The optimized plan serves all 46 pickup locations with five vehicles, compared with 22 locations served by seven vehicles in the existing operation, and reduces distance per served point from 14.57 to 4.08 km/point while keeping the longest route at 144 minutes. The case also reveals a transferable operational pattern: early routes tend to be filled efficiently in demand-concentrated areas, whereas residual spatially dispersed demand tends to create lower-utilization tail routes. A fixed-seed Genetic Algorithm benchmark further reduced total distance to 152.79 km under the same constraints, but required a longer average runtime of 60.52 seconds compared with 1.13 seconds for the proposed MATLAB-based heuristic. These findings show that transparent classical heuristics can still deliver implementable gains in urban pickup logistics when capacity and time feasibility are evaluated jointly.

title: A Machine Learning Approach for Cassava Leaf Disease Identification Using Constraint-Regularized Neural Networks and AJFO Meta-Optimization
abstract: Early diagnosis of cassava leaf diseases is paramount to enhance the productivity of cassava and to support sustainable agriculture. Traditional deep learning methods, however, are not very robust in complex field conditions, suffer from manual hyperparameter tuning, and are not fully leveraging the structural information from the disease, which leads to poor classification accuracy and poor generalization. To cope with these challenges, this paper proposes a unified machine learning framework for cassava leaf disease identification, which combines with enhanced image preprocessing, Residual Multi-scale U-Net (RMUNet) segmentation, Multi-Level Feature Extraction (MLFE), Constraint-Regularized Neural Network (CRNN), and Artificial Jellyfish Optimization (AJFO). The proposed approach is different from the conventional RMUNet-based disease detection techniques, which involve disease-oriented multiscale segmentation along with structural regularization in feature space to enhance the classification resilience in the presence of illumination variations, background clutter, and noisy farming ground. Moreover, AJFO uses to tune the learning rate, batch size, dropout rate, training epochs, and regularization coefficient in an automatic way, which removes the manual tuning of these parameters and increases the stability of convergence. A computational complexity analysis also shows that the extra cost of optimization is only during offline training, and inference complexity is comparable to the conventional deep learning models. Experimental results on the Cassava Leaf Disease dataset show the effectiveness of the proposed framework with 99% classification accuracy for healthy leaves, 97% classification accuracy for Cassava Mosaic Disease (CMD), 95% classification accuracy for Cassava Green Mite (CGM), and 93% classification accuracy for Cassava Brown Streak Disease (CBSD) and consistently better precision, recall, and F1-score than CNN-PLDD, SVM-PLDD, and DENN-PLDD. Overall, the proposed integrated framework demonstrates its capability of achieving effective convergence, better generalization performance, and effective disease classification performance under different imaging conditions, which is considered as a strong solution for intelligent precision agriculture and automated crop health monitoring.

title: Early-Time Filtrate Invasion Modeling During Primary Drilling-In of Terrigenous Oil Reservoirs
abstract: Accurate interpretation of geological and technological data acquired during drilling largely depends on understanding the interaction between drilling fluid and the productive formation at the initial stage of reservoir penetration. One of the least investigated phenomena affecting the reliability of well logging and gas logging interpretation is ahead-of-bit filtration, in which drilling fluid filtrate invades the formation before its physical exposure by the drill bit. This study aims to develop the scientific basis for a methodology to calculate the parameters of the formation fluid displacement front caused by ahead-of-bit filtration during the primary penetration of terrigenous oil-bearing reservoirs. The proposed methodology combines an analytical description of drilling fluid spurt loss with a two-phase flow model to predict filtrate invasion under downhole conditions. An algorithm was developed to calculate the principal parameters governing the displacement process along the wellbore axis, including filtrate invasion volume, filtrate saturation, penetration depth, and the position of the formation fluid displacement front. The analytical formulation enables laboratory and bench-scale filtration data to be extrapolated to actual drilling conditions, thereby improving the prediction of filtrate invasion during reservoir penetration. The developed approach provides a quantitative framework for evaluating the influence of ahead-of-bit filtration on reservoir fluid saturation and the interpretation of gas logging measurements obtained from drilled cuttings. Application of the proposed methodology demonstrated that the presence of drilling fluid filtrate leads to an underestimation of the native fluid saturation, with the filtrate fraction reaching 4.35% in the investigated case. The proposed methodology offers an effective tool for improving the interpretation accuracy of geological and technological drilling data and supports more reliable characterization of productive formations during the primary penetration stage.

title: Automated Indentation Geometry Detection for Hardness Measurement: A Vision-Based Nondestructive Evaluation Approach
abstract: Hardness testing is one of the most widely applied methods for evaluating the mechanical properties of metallic materials in manufacturing and quality control. Among standardized techniques, Brinell, Vickers, and Rockwell are most commonly used, all relying on precise measurement of indentation geometry. However, conventional evaluation methods still depend on manual or semi-automated readings, which are prone to operator error and unsuitable for industrial automation. This study introduces an automated framework for indentation geometry detection and measurement using two complementary strategies: a classical image processing pipeline based on OpenCV and a YOLOv10n deep learning model. To replicate realistic industrial conditions, St37 steel blocks with unpolished, roughly machined surfaces and random markings were tested under Brinell, Vickers, and Rockwell A hardness standards. A batch of microscope images was gathered, manually annotated, and subsequently expanded via data augmentation to obtain a diverse and reliable labeled image set. The classical pipeline employed brightness enhancement, thresholding, morphological filtering, and contour-based geometry extraction, while YOLOv10n was trained on the augmented dataset and refined using geometry-based post-processing. The YOLOv10n model achieved a mean average precision (detection accuracy) of 94% and reduced mean absolute error by 42–51% compared with classical image processing (p < 0.05). Furthermore, it maintained 96–97% accuracy under brightness variation, rotation, and mirroring, whereas the classical approach deteriorated to 79–84%. YOLOv10n provides a robust, precise, and scalable solution for automated hardness testing, supporting the advancement of automation in industrial quality control.

title: Finite-Element Assessment of Concrete Mine-Shaft Lining: Lamé Validation and Groove Effects
abstract: This paper presents a Lamé-verified finite-element workflow for assessing the stress–strain state and residual load-bearing capacity of concrete linings in vertical mine shafts with local technological grooves. A full three-dimensional 1 m high lining ring with an internal diameter of 6 m was modeled in Abaqus and verified against the analytical Lamé solution for a thick-walled cylinder under external pressure. Four scenarios were analyzed: an elastic intact reference model, an elastic model with an inner technological recess, a zonal concrete damage-plasticity model (CDPM2) without groove, and a zonal CDPM2 model with groove. The radial and hoop stress profiles closely matched the analytical solution. The groove caused pronounced stress redistribution, including a tensile hoop-stress concentration of approximately 24 MPa on the outer side of the lining opposite the groove and inner-contour ovalization with radial displacement from −9.0 to +7.4 mm. A parametric post-processing campaign evaluated groove depth, groove radius/opening, mesh density, concrete class, and zonal material assumptions using the normalized residual-capacity indicator R_FE. Groove depth governed the global residual-capacity trend, whereas groove radius/opening acted as a secondary geometric modifier. The Abaqus internal energy output (ALLIE) and dissipated/stabilization energy output (ALLSD) are interpreted as comparative energy indicators, not standalone failure criteria. The workflow connects finite-element assessment with field diagnostics while acknowledging limitations related to local peak-stress convergence, low-pressure proxy interpretation, and the adopted CDPM2 parameterization.

title: Prediction of Structural Defects During Solidification of Al-Si-Mg Alloy System by Scheil-Gulliver Method
abstract: This study applies Scheil-Gulliver non-equilibrium solidification modeling, implemented in ProCAST 13.5.2 with the AlDATA 4.2 thermodynamic database, to predict defect-promoting intermetallic phase formation in an AlSi9Mg alloy (Si 9.2, Mg 0.45, Ni 0.19, Fe 0.2, Mn 0.3 wt.%) derived from automotive scrap remelting in Cuba. The model predicts solidification between 597 and 533 °C a 65 °C non-equilibrium window with a phase formation sequence that places brittle Al3Ni needles first, followed by Mg2Si and the π-phase (Al8FeMg3Si6) during eutectic arrest at ~558 °C. Predicted phase fractions reach 0.022, 0.081, and 0.048 wt.% respectively. All representing upper-bound estimates under the no-back-diffusion assumption. Computed thermophysical properties showed that thermal conductivity dropped 67 W/m·K across the solidification interval, while density decreased by 200 kg/m³, both critical inputs for shrinkage-porosity prediction. The Mn/Fe ratio of 1.5 in this alloy suppresses the formation of β-Al5FeSi in favor of less detrimental Al15(Fe, Mn)3Si2, a result the model captures without additional fitting parameters. Practical thresholds for Ni content, Mg/Si ratio, and cooling rate control are derived from the simulation and validated against published experimental data for comparable alloy systems. The results demonstrate that Scheil-Gulliver modeling with industrial-grade thermodynamic databases provides actionable guidance for secondary aluminum foundry operations where compositional variability is inherent.

title: Analysis the Characteristics and Performance of Polyethersulfone-Carbon Nanotube Membranes Fabricated Using Electric Field Method for Water Filtration Applications
abstract: This study aims to address the effect of Carbon Nanotube (CNT) addition on the characteristics and performance of polyethersulfone (PES) membranes fabricated using the Electric Field method. Four PES membranes were fabricated with addition of CNT and denoted as SM0 (0% CNT), SM1 (0.5% CNT), SM2 (1% CNT), and SM3 (1.5% CNT). SEM observations showed average pore sizes of 0.62±0.12 μm to 0.82±0.18 μm, and AFM images showed the ability of CNTs to increase topographical complexity. The tensile test results indicated that addition of CNT increased the tensile strength of the membrane. The TGA and DTG test graphs showed that addition of CNT can increase the thermal resistance of the membrane. FTIR spectra were in agreement with characteristic PES functional groups. The XRD data showed that the amorphous nature remains dominant, indicating that this composite membrane successfully combines the mechanical strength and functional properties of CNTs without sacrificing the intrinsic pore structure of the PES polymer. Addition of CNT to the membrane increased its hydrophilicity, as evidenced by decrease in water contact angle on the membrane. Addition of CNT can also increase the membrane permeability, as indicated by an increase in the membrane permeability values in the range of 1 to 6 bar. In terms of durability, adding CNT to the membrane can increase its durability, meaning that membranes with added CNT can last longer than pure PES membranes.

title: Deep Learning–Based Multimodal Fusion of Wavelet-Decomposed MRI and PET for Alzheimer’s Disease Diagnosis
abstract: Early and accurate diagnosis of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is crucial for timely clinical intervention and treatment planning. Recent advances in deep learning have facilitated the automatic extraction of informative biomarkers from neuroimaging data. In this study, we proposed a multimodal framework that integrates structural magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and functional positron emission tomography (PET) using three-dimensional convolutional neural networks (3D-CNNs) with wavelet-domain feature extraction (CO.2). First, MRI and PET volumes are decomposed into multiple sub-bands via discrete wavelet transform (DWT) to capture complementary frequency-domain patterns. Next, a custom 3D-CNN extracts multi-scale hierarchical features from each modality (CO.3,4). The resulting modality-specific embeddings are fused at the decision level through a stacked one-dimensional CNN (1D-CNN) ensemble to classify subjects into AD, mild cognitive impairment (MCI), and normal control (NC) groups. Experiments on the ADNI dataset show strong performance across three binary tasks, achieving 97.9% (AD vs. NC), 97.5% (MCI vs. NC), and 99.6% (AD vs. MCI, AUC ≈ 0.997). These results demonstrate that the proposed wavelet-enhanced stacked multimodal model provides a robust and generalizable tool for early-stage AD detection, particularly in distinguishing subtle transitions between MCI and AD (CO.2).

title: The Legal Foundations for the Evolving Role of Oversight Bodies in Combating Corruption in Iraq
abstract: This research aims to elucidate the legal foundations upon which the evolving role of oversight bodies in combating corruption in Iraq is based. This is achieved through an analysis of the constitutional and legislative framework governing their operations, and by examining the impact of legal and constitutional developments, particularly the 2005 Constitution of the Republic of Iraq, on strengthening their jurisdictions and powers. Furthermore, the research studies the influence of international agreements, primarily the United Nations Convention against Corruption, on the development of the Iraqi oversight system. The research's significance lies in its focus on a topic directly related to protecting public funds and establishing the principles of integrity, transparency, and accountability. This is accomplished by assessing the adequacy of the legal framework governing oversight bodies in addressing corruption, thereby contributing to the development of national legislation and enhancing the effectiveness of oversight institutions in achieving good governance. To this end, the research employs a descriptive-analytical approach to examine and analyze constitutional and legislative texts, a historical approach to trace the evolution of oversight bodies in Iraq, and an inductive approach to derive the legal principles governing their work. The research concluded that the development of the role of oversight bodies was based on a set of constitutional and legislative foundations that strengthened their legal standing and expanded their mandates in combating corruption. However, the persistence of certain challenges, most notably overlapping jurisdictions, weak institutional coordination, the need to enhance administrative and financial independence, and the need to update legislation to keep pace with emerging forms of corruption, necessitates continued legislative and institutional reform. This will achieve a more efficient and effective oversight system for protecting public funds and upholding the rule of law.

title: Evaluating Credit Score Explanations in Lending Decisions and Risk Management
abstract: Credit score explanations can influence lending reviews, exception handling, and customer communication, yet an explanation may change under resampling, recommend an infeasible action, or fail to illuminate the approval decision.This structured review examines the evidence needed to use explanations in lending and risk management.Thirty-eight journal studies published from 2023 through January 2026 were coded by method family, information setting, validation design, and decision connection.The evidence spans interpretable scores and rules, post hoc attributions, counterfactuals, stability tests, fairness audits, and decision-oriented comparators.It does not support a single ranking of methods: studies examine different properties on different applicant populations, and few identify the incremental effect of an explanation on an underwriter's action or an applicant's outcome.Four comparisons organize the findings.Predictive discrimination does not establish explanation fidelity; plausible local reasons may not survive changes in training data; a score-changing counterfactual may be unattainable; and similar attributions do not imply equal lending outcomes.We develop a validation framework linking temporal performance, explanation perturbations, feasible action, group analysis, and policy value.Additional analyses map the evidence to decision stages, distinguish estimable quantities from missing outcomes, and specify reporting standards for management use.The review contributes an operational basis for deciding when an explanation can be treated as evidence in underwriting rather than as a model display.

title: From Demand Signals to Retail Decisions in Business Intelligence Research
abstract: Retail analytics has moved beyond improving point forecasts, yet evidence about the value of a forecast for pricing, replenishment, fulfillment, and managerial adoption remains dispersed.This structured review compares 36 journal studies published from 2023 through 2025, identified within a search window ending in January 2026, across four connected areas: demand forecasting (12), pricing and commercial levers (7), inventory and fulfillment (8), and decision systems (9).Each study is examined for its information setting, analytic approach, decision connection, and evidence boundary.The synthesis identifies four recurring discontinuities: sales data can conceal unmet demand; forecast scores can misrank policies; a policy that works in a model may be infeasible in a distributed retail organization; and staff may override recommendations whose value has not been made legible.A decision-centered evaluation structure links data availability, uncertainty estimation, feasible action, adoption, and realized economic outcomes.The paper develops a research agenda around observable-demand corrections, decision-calibrated uncertainty, joint pricing and fulfillment, transportable evaluations, and human-in-the-loop deployment.The review is deliberately bounded rather than a claim of exhaustive coverage or pooled effect sizes.It offers business intelligence researchers a common basis for studying whether analytical improvements survive the operational decisions they are meant to inform.

title: Drone Threats to Nuclear Installations During Armed Conflict: Risk-Based Protection Strategies
abstract: The growing use of unmanned aircraft systems in armed conflict has created new nuclear security challenges for nuclear installations. Drones may support surveillance, unauthorized airspace intrusion, smuggling, operational disruption, and attacks on supporting infrastructure. Their small size, low-altitude operation, increasing autonomy, and evolving payload capacity complicate detection, attribution, and timely response. Fiber-optic-controlled drones add a further challenge because they can reduce the effectiveness of conventional counter-drone measures, particularly radio-frequency detection, jamming, and operator geolocation. This study examines drone threats to nuclear installations during armed conflict and proposes a risk-based framework for strengthening nuclear security resilience. Using a qualitative approach based on international nuclear security guidance, counter-drone literature, and documented conflict-related cases, the framework assesses risk through four variables: threat likelihood, vulnerability, consequence, and protection readiness. The framework is applied to incidents involving the Zaporizhzhia and Chornobyl nuclear facilities. The study finds that effective protection requires layered detection, integrated counter-drone procedures, resilient safety and security systems, legal preparedness, and coordinated response among operators, regulators, law enforcement, military authorities, aviation agencies, and emergency services. The paper contributes a non-sensitive analytical model for evaluating and managing drone threats to nuclear installations in conflict environments.

title: Modelling the Dynamics between Life Expectancy, Economic Growth, Renewable Energy Transition, and Carbon Footprints in BRICS Economies
abstract: With rapid economic growth in BRICS, significant concerns about sustainability and climate change have emerged. However, changing demographics, longer lifespans, and the growing adoption of renewable energy have shifted growth’s environmental impacts. Using a panel Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) approach, robust cointegration analyses establish the long-run relationship between the constructs. The ARDL panel estimates that higher economic growth (GDP) indicates greater affluence, which, along with population growth, has positive long-run effects and therefore increases CO2 emissions. However, these effects were offset by the adverse effects of increased renewable energy consumption, which reflects technological progress, and life expectancy, which reflects demographic transition, in controlling emissions. In contrast, the causality analysis provides evidence of bidirectional causality between GDP and CO2 emissions, suggesting a complex interaction. Furthermore, this study finds that renewable energy consumption, population growth, and life expectancy individually have unidirectional causal effects on CO2 emissions. Robustness estimates using fully modified ordinary least squares (FMOLS) and dynamic ordinary least squares (DOLS) support the ARDL hypothesis. These results support the applicability of the Impact = Population × Affluence × Technology (IPAT) model, with proper consideration of the mutual interactions among population, affluence, and technology in determining the key drivers of ecological impact.

title: Directional Robustness Asymmetry in Indonesian Sarcasm Detection: A Cross-Platform Evaluation of IndoRoBERTa on X and Reddit
abstract: Sarcasm can reverse sentence polarity, making it one of the hardest problems in natural language processing and a persistent obstacle to reliable sentiment analysis on social media, where models are often deployed on platforms they were not trained on. Research on Indonesian sarcasm has largely stayed within a single domain or tested transfer in only one direction, leaving the cross-domain robustness of the IndoRoBERTa family on the IdSarcasm benchmark unclear. This study measures and compares the cross-domain robustness of IndoRoBERTa-small and IndoRoBERTa-base, with IndoBERT as a baseline, across X (Twitter) and Reddit, using the F1 gap (ΔF1) after cleaning anonymization artifacts, adding a data-size control, and running Stratified 5-Fold cross-validation. The results reveal a one-sided asymmetry: X → Reddit transfer is far more fragile (ΔF1 0.345–0.400) than Reddit → X (0.135–0.240), failing by missing sarcasm (false negatives) rather than over-flagging it (false positives). Practically, training on the context-rich domain (Reddit) and choosing IndoRoBERTa-base give the most reliable cross-platform sarcasm detection, with direction-specific mitigation recommended for robust deployment.

title: A Comparative Analysis of the Application of Circumstantial Evidence in the Criminal Systems of Iran and Egypt and Islamic Jurisprudence
abstract: Circumstantial evidence, as an important instrument of indirect proof in criminal proceedings, plays a fundamental role in discovering truth, establishing judicial knowledge, and achieving criminal justice. The transformation of criminal behavior and the limitations of traditional evidentiary mechanisms have increased the importance of material, moral, scientific, and electronic indications in contemporary legal systems. The present study aimed to comparatively analyze the application of circumstantial evidence in the criminal systems of Iran and Egypt and Islamic jurisprudence. Using a descriptive-analytical method and a comparative approach, this study examined the jurisprudential and legal foundations of circumstantial evidence, its position in criminal proof, and the limitations of its application. The findings indicated that, in Islamic jurisprudence, the validity of circumstantial evidence depends on the type of crime, its degree of certainty, and its compatibility with principles such as the presumption of innocence and the rule of avoiding hudud punishments in doubtful cases. In hudud crimes, the use of circumstantial evidence is more restricted due to the necessity of caution and prevention of unjust convictions, whereas in ta’zir crimes, it has broader applicability. In the Iranian criminal system, circumstantial evidence mainly obtains validity through the formation of judicial knowledge and must be based on objective, assessable, and case-related evidence. Conversely, the Egyptian criminal system, through its emphasis on judicial persuasion, provides greater flexibility in evaluating circumstantial evidence, although judicial decisions must remain reasoned and evidence-based. The comparison demonstrates that the main difference between the two systems is not the acceptance of circumstantial evidence itself but the theoretical foundation and method of applying it. Ultimately, the effective use of circumstantial evidence requires a balance between truth discovery, modern evidentiary developments, and protection of defendants’ rights.

title: Impact of Digital Construction Technologies on Sustainability Awareness and Decision-Making in Civil Engineering Education
abstract: Digital technologies such as Building Information Modeling (BIM), Artificial Intelligence (AI), simulation platforms, and virtual and augmented reality are reshaping civil engineering education, yet their influence on sustainability awareness and decision-making is not well understood. This study surveyed 73 students enrolled in civil engineering courses at a public university in the southeastern United States. The instrument comprised 36 Likert-scale statements, grouped into eight constructs covering technology use in the curriculum, professional mindset, sustainability knowledge and lifecycle and environmental awareness. They also covered understanding of water resources, cognitive ability, emotional intelligence, and problem-solving. It also includes three decision scenarios in which a digital tool output conflicted with human input or practical constraints. Students reported favorable attitudes toward digital tools, along with strong conceptual sustainability awareness, but two applied-skill gaps stood out: only 32.9% felt able to interpret hydrologic models, and only 28.8% felt they could transfer simulation-based lessons to real world settings. In the scenarios, at most 12.3% of respondents accepted the digital output at face value, and 83.6% never did so across all three scenarios. Breadth of tool exposure was unrelated to perceptions or decision style, whereas the small group of students reporting exposure to hydrologic modeling rated their model interpretation ability substantially higher, suggesting that relevant depth matters more than the number of tools encountered. The findings support curricula that pair earlier and deeper BIM and hydrologic modeling instruction with lifecycle content and that train verification and interpretation skills alongside tool operation.

title: From Authorship to Accountability - Rethinking Copyright Governance for AI-Generated Art
abstract: This study examines how the rapid expansion of generative artificial intelligence (AI) challenges traditional copyright law by shifting legal concerns beyond authorship and ownership toward transparency, disclosure, traceability, and accountability in AI-assisted artistic production.The study adopts a doctrinal and comparative legal methodology to analyse copyright principles, emerging regulatory frameworks, and policy developments relating to AI-generated content. Particular attention is given to the European Union Artificial Intelligence Act, international copyright debates, and the Albanian legal framework under Law No. 35/2016 “On Copyright and Related Rights”.The analysis demonstrates that existing copyright regimes remain predominantly authorship-centred and provide limited guidance regarding accountability when AI systems contribute to artistic creation. Significant regulatory gaps persist concerning disclosure obligations, traceability of AI involvement, transparency of creative processes, and the allocation of responsibility among users, developers, and platform providers. The findings further indicate that accountabilitybased governance offers a valuable complement to traditional copyright doctrines in addressing the challenges of AI-assisted creativity. The study is limited to legal JUS & JUSTICIA No. 20, ISSUE 2/ 2026 95 and regulatory analysis and does not incorporate empirical evidence from creators, policymakers, technology developers, or judicial practice in Albania. Future research may benefit from examining stakeholder perspectives and the practical implementation of emerging AI governance frameworks. The findings support the development of governance mechanisms based on mandatory disclosure of AI involvement, documentation of human creative contribution, enhanced transparency standards, and traceability measures for AI-generated artistic content. These measures may strengthen legal certainty and improve copyright enforcement in AIassisted creative environments.The study contributes to current scholarship by moving beyond the traditional debate on authorship and copyrightability and proposing an accountability-oriented framework for copyright governance. It offers one of the first analyses linking transparency, disclosure, traceability, and accountability principles to the regulation of AI-generated art within both the Albanian and European legal contexts.

title: Public Procurement, European Integration and Sustainable Economic Development – The Cases of Croatia, Albania, the Czech Republic, and Romania
abstract: This study examines public procurement’s role in European integration and sustainable economic development across four post-socialist European countries: Croatia, Albania, the Czech Republic, and Romania. Relying on EU reports, technical documents, and other international sources, the analysis in this paper explores the progress and challenges in aligning legal and institutional procurement frameworks with EU standards, as well as their contribution to transparency, anti-corruption efforts, innovation, and sustainable economic development. Particular attention is paid to the strategic function of public procurement, which remains unevenly developed across the cases, particularly in Albania and Romania, thereby weakening the connection between public procurement planning and broader sustainable development goals. The findings suggest that despite formal harmonization with EU legislation, the implementation of good governance principles and strategic approaches remains challenging, especially where implementation capacity remains uneven, as in Albania and Romania.

title: Radiological Diagnosis of Lung Diseases Using Artificial Intelligence: A Study Guide
abstract: В учебном пособии рассмотрены лучевые методы выявления и диагностики заболеваний легких — с этапа проверочной флюорографии как скрининга населения на своевременное выявление туберкулеза до лучевой диагностики при обращении пациента в лечебные учреждения, в том числе с жалобами респираторного характера. Впервые в пособии материал подается с позиции внедрения в рутинную практику технологий искусственного интеллекта в распознавании лучевых изображений. Для оценки работы искусственного интеллекта в распознавании лучевых изображений даны основы знаний в лучевой диагностике, представления о применяемых цифровых технологиях, компьютерного зрения, адаптированных для специфики рентгенологических изображений органов грудной клетки с большим набором данных по результатам внедрения в практическое здравоохранение. Издание предназначено студентам медицинских вузов, врачам общей практики, терапевтам, пульмонологам, фтизиатрам, проходящим обучение в системе послевузовского образования.

title: Few-shot semantic segmentation of UAV imagery for plant conservation: A systematic comparison of foundation models for Euphorbia resinifera mapping
abstract: Deep learning has transformed vegetation mapping from UAV imagery, yet state-of-the-art segmentation models require hundreds to thousands of expertly annotated images, creating prohibitive labor costs for conservation applications targeting endangered flora. This study addresses this bottleneck by systematically comparing three foundation models namely: DINOv2 (self-supervised), SegGPT (supervised), and SAM (promptable), for binary segmentation of Euphorbia resinifera, an endemic Moroccan succulent of conservation concern, using patches extracted from a single annotated UAV orthomosaic. A single-image training framework is presented where spatial diversity within one high-resolution orthomosaic substitutes for diversity across multiple images, combined with sliding window inference with vote-based fusion for full-resolution deployment. SegGPT achieved 83.74±2.55% mean IoU across 20 spatially independent test images spanning a 10.5-fold vegetation density gradient (2.01 to 21.11% coverage), outperforming DINOv2 (78.09±6.63%) and SAM (47.03±20.64%). The observed collapse in SAM’s performance, despite billion-mask pretraining, can be attributed to its architectural constraints. SAM’s fixed 1024×1024 input reduced training patches by 76.2%, and its frozen encoder limited trainable parameters to 0.1M versus SegGPT’s 316M. These findings establish that fine-tuned encoders substantially outperform frozen-encoder architectures for specialized vegetation (Euphorbia resinifera) segmentation, and that single-image foundation model training offers a viable paradigm for conservation deployment, reducing annotation costs from tens of thousands to hundreds of dollars. While demonstrated for a morphologically distinctive species, these principles may inform broader conservation remote sensing applications pending validation across diverse plant forms.

title: El modelo pedagógico de innovación crítica: metodología para el fortalecimiento del conocimiento y el aprendizaje en los estudiantes de pregrado
abstract: Background. Pedagogical innovation is one of the main challenges facing higher education in the twenty-first century, as digital transformation now shapes every mode of instruction and calls into question the way students build knowledge. Objective. To develop an emerging pedagogical model that strengthens knowledge and learning among undergraduate students, drawing on the experiences of students, faculty, and administrators across different educational modes. Methods. A qualitative study was conducted under the interpretive-critical paradigm using a grounded theory design. A total of 221 participants from three Colombian institutions representing on-campus, military on-campus, and online modes were selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews, supported by document analysis of reports issued by the Colombian Ministry of National Education and by observational research. The analysis involved open, axial, and selective coding, source triangulation, and categorical convergence analysis. Results. Eight emerging categories were identified: pedagogical innovation as the organizing axis, participation and dialogue, reflective assessment, critical thinking, faculty development, educational equity, meaningful learning, and the pedagogical use of artificial intelligence and ICT. The three groups agreed that changing educational practice depends not on adopting technology or making isolated methodological changes, but on aligning pedagogy, didactics, teaching strategies, and the instructional context. Conclusions. The convergence of these categories gives rise to the Pedagogical Model of Critical Innovation, an emerging theoretical construct that offers a conceptual reference for updating institutional education projects, pedagogical models, and curriculum designs across the different modes of higher education.

title: Designing and Explaining a Model of Managerial Behavioral Integrity in the North Khorasan Governorate
abstract: This study aimed to design and explain a model of managerial behavioral integrity in the North Khorasan Governorate by identifying its causal, contextual, and intervening conditions, strategies, and consequences. This exploratory and developmental study employed a qualitative design based on the systematic grounded theory approach of Strauss and Corbin. The study population consisted of managers and employees of the North Khorasan Governorate with more than 10 years of work experience. Participants were selected using purposive sampling, and sampling continued until theoretical saturation was achieved, resulting in 20 participants. Data were collected through in-depth semi-structured interviews and analysis of organizational documents. Data analysis was conducted through open, axial, and selective coding, and the extracted concepts were organized into causal conditions, the central phenomenon, contextual conditions, intervening conditions, strategies, and consequences. To assess coding dependability, selected interviews were independently coded by a research colleague. Cohen’s kappa coefficient was 0.87, indicating a very high level of inter-coder agreement. The analysis identified managerial behavioral integrity as the central phenomenon of the model. Stability and consistency of managerial actions and acceptance of mistakes and moral courage emerged as causal conditions. Transparency and fairness in decision-making, together with effective communication and team cohesion, constituted the contextual conditions. Empathy and employee support and the prevention of distrust and inappropriate behavior were identified as intervening conditions. The principal strategies were strengthening a positive organizational culture and enhancing employee motivation and participation. The consequences of implementing the model included increased organizational trust and psychological safety, reduced tension, conflict, and job burnout, enhanced employee motivation and participation, stronger organizational belonging and team cohesion, and improved managerial credibility. Managerial behavioral integrity is a multidimensional and context-dependent phenomenon shaped by the interaction of managerial behavior, organizational conditions, and manager–employee relationships; therefore, strengthening transparency, accountability, word–deed alignment, fairness, moral courage, and employee participation can contribute to greater organizational trust, administrative integrity, and effectiveness in public-sector organizations.

title: No Species Is an Island, Entire of Itself: Genetic Speciation Algorithm with Interplay among Species
abstract: This paper, with a particular emphasis on Genetic Algorithm (GA), proposes a novel approach that integrates clustering mechanisms, predator-prey dynamics, and a distinctive selection strategy for generating subsequent populations. The proposed evolutionary algorithm, referred to as Genetic Speciation Algorithm with Interplay Among Species (GSAIS), is comprehensively evaluated against several variants of GAs as well as a set of widely adopted state-of-the-art optimization algorithms, recognized among the top-performing winners of recent Congress on Evolutionary Computation (CEC) competitions. This thorough comparative study is performed using the most well-established benchmark functions, covering unimodal, multimodal, hybrid, and composition optimization landscapes. The experiments are conducted on medium-, and large-scale problem instances to evaluate the robustness, scalability, convergence behavior, and solution quality of GSAIS across diverse optimization scenarios. The GSAIS achieved rank 2nd, and 1st against the competitors in medium- and large- scale benchmark problems, respectively based on the Friedman Test with receiving 40.3% of top ranking along all instances based on best found and standard deviation rankings. Extensive statistical and computational results demonstrate the effectiveness of GSAIS, highlighting its superior performance in achieving global optimization. The ablation study and sensitivity analysis reveals the positive effect of the incorporated mechanisms in GSAIS in finding global optimization, especially in large scale problems. The findings establish GSAIS as a potential candidate method for addressing optimization problems and underscore its potential to advance the design of next-generation evolutionary algorithms.

title: Three-Dimensional Thermomechanical Analysis of Radial Friction Welding of Dissimilar Copper-Aluminum Alloys: Finite Element Modelling and Experimental Validation
abstract: This study investigates radial friction welding of dissimilar AA2024 aluminum and Cu-DHP copper using a three-dimensional finite element model together with optical metallography, Vickers microhardness measurements, and thermocouple measurements. A coupled thermomechanical model was implemented in ANSYS Workbench 2023 R1 at 1 400 rpm and 30 MPa. The numerical solution predicts an asymmetric thermal field with a maximum of 750 °C at the Al-Cu interface, an equivalent plastic strain of 0.0177 mm/mm, and a maximum total displacement of 0.130 mm. The strain and displacement fields were interpreted together with the optical observations, which indicate localized thermomechanical modification and preferential material flow near the interface. The thermomechanically affected zone (TMAZ) reached approximately 157 HV. Direct comparison with thermocouple measurements and the measured aluminum-side TMAZ width supported the model for the directly comparable quantities. Microhardness provides complementary evidence of localized hardening but does not constitute direct strain measurement or phase identification. The model is useful for interpreting the thermomechanical response of AA2024/Cu-DHP radial friction welds, while the assumptions regarding friction and radiation, the absence of latent heat, and the absence of microstructural-kinetics modelling remain explicit limitations.

title: Comparative Analysis of Applied Approaches to Monitoring the Technical Condition and Performance of Electric Submersible Pumps
abstract: This paper aims to provide a comprehensive review of existing methods for diagnosing and predicting failures in electric submersible pumps (ESPs), along with an analysis of their key characteristics, advantages, and limitations. The study presents a structured analysis of publications focused on approaches to fault detection and failure prediction in ESP operations, with particular emphasis on the practical application of the described techniques. Based on the literature analysis, all identified methods are classified into four categories: deterministic, expert-based, data-driven, and hybrid approaches. For each group, implementation examples are given, along with descriptions of their benefits, application areas, and potential limitations. An analysis of 53 scientific articles revealed that deterministic approaches offer a high level of interpretability and are independent of historical data, but require considerable resources to adapt to changing operational conditions. Expert-based approaches, including fuzzy logic systems, are effective in evaluating the current state of equipment, but have limited capabilities for long-term forecasting. Data-driven approaches eliminate the need for physical modeling, but their accuracy depends heavily on the quality and completeness of the input data. The most effective solutions are hybrid approaches that combine the strengths of the aforementioned methods, offering high flexibility and adaptability under various operating conditions.
