title: PoCA-Mithril: A Blockchain-enabled Framework for Identity- and Context-verifiable Communication among Distributed AI Agents
abstract: Distributed Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems face challenges in agent identity verification, context integrity, traceability, and scalable blockchain anchoring without a continuously trusted central authority.This paper proposes PoCA-Mithril, a blockchain framework for verifiable agent communication.Proof-of-Context Attestation (PoCA) signs agent identity, context, timestamp, and safety metadata.A Mithril-Inspired Relay (MR) batches proofs via Merkle trees and a SHA-256 signature digest before Solidity smart-contract anchoring.Prototype (Python, Web3.py, decentralized identifiers, Ganache, web interface) averaged 1.2555, 1.9402, and 3.5815 ms for Elliptic Curve Digital Signature Algorithm (ECDSA) keypair generation, PoCA generation, and verification.Relay aggregation stays below 0.04 ms; five-proof batching cuts transactions 80%.It authenticates identity and context metadata, not complete response-content integrity.Persistent request-ID storage with database-enforced uniqueness rejects duplicates; restart and shared-database tests confirmed persistence.Five-process concurrency yielded one accepted claim, four duplicate rejections; multi-server verification remains unevaluated.An AgentDID-inspired baseline and 10,000-operation workloads characterize the local prototype, not distributed-blockchain performance.Response-content binding, model artifact, and runtime-execution verification remain future work.

title: Adversarial Graph Neural Diffusion for Zero-Day Network Anomaly Detection: A Controlled Evaluation
abstract: Zero-day intrusions cannot be matched against signatures, so a detector must judge whether a host is behaving abnormally rather than whether it matches a known attack.Continuous-depth graph neural networks that treat message passing as a diffusion process have advanced node classification, and this paper asks whether they transfer to host-level anomaly detection.We present AGND, which combines graph neural diffusion with a time-aware attention operator whose diffusivity decays with the time since two hosts last communicated, and with an adversarial generator that synthesises pseudo-anomalous behaviour.On a controlled benchmark of 1440 windows, 100 hosts and 140 attack episodes from six unseen families, evaluated over 10 independently generated networks, AGND reaches 0.939 AUC-ROC and 0.270 AUC-PR under the original protocol and 0.937 and 0.254 under the corrected protocol of attack-free training and label-free selection.Neither proposed component changes this, and removing the diffusion raises AUC-PR to 0.352 and 0.307 respectively.Isolation forests and one-class support vector machines on the same features exceed every graph model on AUC-PR and a two-layer autoencoder matches the best of them, and the ordering survives training on attack-free windows only, label-free model selection and family-held-out selection.A factorial ablation shows that two hand-engineered relational summaries, not learned graph context, carry the relational signal: without them every method loses between 35 and 60 per cent of its AUC-PR, graph models included.Sweeps of depth, source weight and horizon over all networks show that a single Euler step matches the discrete model, that the loss appears at the second step together with a drop in Dirichlet energy, and that changing the energy through the horizon alone leaves detection quality unchanged, so oversmoothing is part of the mechanism rather than the whole of it.A host-window experiment on CIC-IDS2017 traffic reproduces the absence of a graph advantage but not the diffusion penalty.We report a negative result with a bounded explanation.

title: Drift-triggered Evidence Switching for Cold-start Interactive Recommendation under Non-stationary Preferences
abstract: A demographic prior serves a new user well and turns harmful once taste drifts.DES-UCB keeps two estimators apart.F is fitted on the user's own feedback since the last detected change.C pools the prior rows with that feedback and is warm LinUCB while nothing moves.A controller picks one of the two when they disagree.On a Page-Hinkley firing the old feedback is dropped, C is rebuilt, its credit is wiped and F runs alone for a burn-in.12 claims were preregistered and 10 hold under one tuning rule and seed-clustered intervals.On abrupt drift with a stale prior the regret is 24.7 against 78.0 without suppression, 73.0 for passive decay and 31.3 for a detector-triggered restart. 2 claims fail.Without drift it costs 1.28 times the regret of warm LinUCB.MovieLens-1M shows no precision gain.The contribution is a mechanism, its diagnostics and a preregistered protocol.

title: MSCK-Net: A Hybrid Multi-scale CNN–KAN–CatBoost Framework for EEG-based Autism Spectrum Disorder Classification
abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental disorder that affects communication, social interaction, and behavioral patterns.Electroencephalography (EEG) signals have been widely employed for ASD diagnosis because they provide valuable information regarding brain activity.However, the complex, nonlinear, highdimensional, and noisy nature of EEG signals makes accurate ASD classification a challenging task.To address these challenges, this study proposes MSCK-Net, a hybrid deep learning (DL) framework that integrates Multi-Scale Convolutional Neural Networks (Multi-Scale CNNs), Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs), and CatBoost classification for EEG-based ASD classification.Initially, EEG features are normalized using Min-Max normalization to ensure consistent feature scaling.Subsequently, Multi-Scale CNN modules extract discriminative EEG representations at different temporal scales, while the KAN module learns nonlinear relationships among the extracted features.Finally, CatBoost performs ASD classification using the learned feature representations.The proposed framework was evaluated using the University of Sheffield EEG Dataset under a subject-independent evaluation protocol.Experimental results demonstrated that the proposed MSCK-Net framework achieved segment-level 99.45% precision, 99.50% F1-score, 99.46% accuracy, and 99.56% recall, while subject-level majority voting correctly classified all 17 held-out subjects (100% accuracy), achieving competitive performance compared with recent EEGbased ASD classification methods while outperforming the evaluated CNN, CNN-LSTM, CNN-GRU, and EEGNet baselines under the adopted experimental protocol.Furthermore, MSCK-Net required 31.2 ms execution time, 5.4 MB model size, and 52.8 MB memory usage, demonstrating a moderate performance-complexity trade-off.Noise analysis under different SNR conditions further assessed the framework's stability.The results demonstrate accurate and robust EEG-based ASD classification under the adopted experimental conditions.

title: Open-set and Hierarchical Lithology Recognition from Rock Photographs for Detecting Unseen Rock Types across Two Public Image Collections
abstract: Rock-type classifiers are usually tested on random splits of one image collection, yet deployed models meet unseen lithologies and new imaging conditions.This evaluation audit merged two public rock-photograph collections into a 15-type, three-family taxonomy and grouped duplicates and augmented copies into 3,521 deduplicated units for group-aware cross-validation of handcrafted features and frozen and fine-tuned ImageNet backbones in closed-set, hierarchical and open-set recognition.A support vector machine reached a macro-F1 of 0.758 under random imagelevel splits and 0.483 when the same images were split by source photograph, so leakage explained almost all of the drop to 0.468 on deduplicated units.In five-fold fine-tuning, ConvNeXt-T and ViT-S/16 reached 0.706 and 0.712 and could not be ranked, and about 45 percent of their errors crossed a family boundary.With score and threshold chosen on validation data only, the AUROC for unseen rock types was 0.625 to 0.748 when training on one collection and 0.734 to 0.815 on the other, while 60 to 97 percent of unknown images were still accepted.Basalt, the only shared type, was scored almost as novel as the unknown types when it came from the other collection, and a probe trained on Basalt alone identified the source collection with an AUROC of 0.94 to 0.95.

title: A U-Mamba-DLKA Framework with Artificial Rabbits Optimization for Automated Liver CT Image Segmentation
abstract: Effective liver segmentation within abdominal computed tomography (CT) scans is an essential requirement for clinical tasks including automated diagnostics, hepatic condition evaluation, and therapeutic progress tracking.However, automatic liver segmentation becomes challenging due to the substantial variations in liver shape and size, indistinct organ boundaries, and the presence of adjacent abdominal structures.Although existing convolutional neural network (CNN)-based and hybrid segmentation models have demonstrated significant performance, many exhibit limited capability in simultaneously capturing long-range contextual dependencies, adaptively refining spatial features, and efficiently optimizing training hyperparameters.To overcome these limitations, this study proposes an optimized liver CT image segmentation framework that integrates a U-Mamba encoder, Deformable Large Kernel Attention (DLKA), and a U-Net decoder within the segmentation architecture, while Artificial Rabbits Optimization (ARO) is employed for automated hyperparameter optimization.The proposed framework employs a hierarchical feature learning strategy in which the U-Mamba encoder combines convolutional operations with selective state-space modelling (SSM) to extract both local anatomical characteristics and long-range contextual dependencies.Subsequently, the DLKA module adaptively refines spatial and contextual feature representations through deformable large-kernel attention to improve contextual understanding and boundary localization, while the U-Net decoder progressively reconstructs high-resolution liver segmentation masks.ARO automatically determines the optimal training hyperparameters, including the learning rate, dropout rate, weight decay, and batch size.The framework was evaluated on the annotated Liver Tumor Segmentation (LiTS) dataset and achieved a Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC) of 96.50%, an Intersection over Union (IoU) of 93.24%, a Precision of 97.12%, a Recall of 95.89%, and a 95th percentile Hausdorff Distance (HD95) of 4.10 mm.Furthermore, the ablation study demonstrated the contribution of the DLKA module and of systematic hyperparameter optimization, the five-fold cross-validation analysis indicated the stability of the selected model configuration, and the comparative analysis with conventional, Mamba-based, and liver-specific segmentation models showed competitive performance under an optimization protocol in which only the proposed framework received hyperparameter search.

title: Cross-attention Guided CNN-Transformer-GNN Architecture for Multi-class Disaster Image Classification
abstract: Disaster image classification emerged as an important research area for supporting rapid disaster assessment, situational awareness, and emergency response operations.Nevertheless, accurately distinguishing among different disaster categories remains challenging due to large intra-class variations, complex backgrounds, and the limited capability of existing approaches to simultaneously capture local visual patterns, global contextual dependencies, and inter-feature relationships.To tackle these challenges, this study proposes a hybrid Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)-Transformer-Graph Neural Network (GNN) approach incorporating a Cross-Attention Gating Block (CAGB) for multi-class disaster image classification.The proposed architecture combines InceptionV3-based convolutional feature extraction with Transformer-based contextual representation learning and Lightweight GNN-based relational feature modeling to generate comprehensive feature representations.Furthermore, the CAGB adaptively refines and integrates heterogeneous features through cross-attention-guided gating, enabling enhanced discrimination among disaster categories.The proposed framework was assessed on a disaster image dataset comprising Cyclone, Earthquake, Flood, and Wildfire classes with 4,428 images.Experimental results demonstrated classification performance, attaining an accuracy of 96.16%, macro-average precision of 96.33%, macro-average recall of 96.10%, macro-average F1-score of 96.20%, and micro-average ROC-AUC of 99.71%.Comparative analysis with existing disaster image classification methods further verified the effectiveness of the proposed approach, highlighting its potential for intelligent disaster monitoring and decision-support applications.

title: Near-duplicate Leakage in Fine-art Classification: A Leakage-controlled Evaluation Protocol and Multi-Seed Benchmark with Perceptual Hash Deduplication
abstract: Random splits of fine-art datasets that contain near-duplicate images inflate accuracy estimates, and ensemble stacking protocols rarely document whether meta-classifier training is free from leakage.We propose and apply a fully documented, leakage-controlled evaluation protocol to the Best Artworks of All Time dataset.Nearduplicates are removed with perceptual hashing (pHash, Hamming ≤ 10; 547 groups, 595 images removed) before any split, and the deduplication is audited on both sides of the threshold (338 pairs; precision 0.97, recall 0.95), which bounds residual train-test duplication at 0.4-1.2% of test images per seed.A seed-matched comparison with nearduplicates retained raises Xception accuracy by 2.47 percentage points (95% CI [0.28, 4.66]), reported as a protocolassociated change rather than as an isolated estimate of cross-split leakage.With the test set held fixed, near-duplicates added only to the training split do not measurably raise accuracy (-0.14 percentage points, 95% CI [-1.58, +1.30], five seeds), and a duplicate-group-aware split that keeps all 4,388 images gives the same accuracy as the deletion policy (+0.42 percentage points, 95% CI [-0.42, +1.26]).As a reference model, four CNN backbones are combined by five-fold out-of-fold stacking with early stopping on an inner validation subset, never on the held-out fold.Over five seeds the ensemble reaches 89.63% (±1.85%) accuracy; by McNemar's test it exceeds ResNet50 in 4 of 5 seeds (3 after Holm correction) and Xception in 3 of 5 (2 after Holm), but not equal-weight soft voting in any seed, and a two-backbone stack reproduces it (89.84%± 1.76%).Under the same protocol Swin-Tiny exceeds the ensemble in every seed (93.74% ± 0.66%; significant in 5 of 5 seeds, 3 after Holm) and ConvNeXtTiny is statistically indistinguishable from it (90.05%± 0.51%); these baselines are architectural representatives of recent methods, not reproductions of them.The contribution is the protocol and the resulting multi-seed benchmark rather than any single model.The conclusions are limited to the defined ten-class benchmark of this collection.

title: HeartFedGAT: An Explainable Federated Multi-scale CNN-Graph Attention Network with Protected Model-update Transmission for Heart Disease Prediction
abstract: Cardiovascular diseases continue to pose a significant worldwide health challenge, underscoring the need for reliable, privacy-conscious prediction models that support timely diagnostic workflows.Although existing methods can capture complex relationships among clinical features, achieving both model interpretability and data privacy remains challenging.To address these issues, this study presents HeartFedGAT, an Explainable Federated Multi-Scale CNN-Graph Attention Network for heart disease prediction.The framework integrates multi-scale convolutional feature extraction, a graph layer with learnable adjacency, graph attention-based feature refinement, Fernet-encrypted model-update transmission with sample-size-weighted Federated Averaging (FedAvg), and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) for model interpretability.The proposed framework was evaluated using the UCI Heart Disease dataset, comprising 3,235 patient records with 14 clinical attributes, distributed across multiple federated clients for collaborative learning.HeartFedGAT achieved a global classification accuracy of 93.35%, alongside high precision, recall, F1-score, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC).An ablation study and comparisons with representative baseline models provided quantitative evidence of the contributions of the major architectural components under the evaluated experimental setting.Furthermore, SHAP analysis identified influential clinical features, supporting the interpretation of model predictions.Overall, the results demonstrate the potential of HeartFedGAT as an explainable and privacy-conscious framework for heart disease prediction in a simulated federated learning setting.However, external validation is required to establish its generalizability and applicability across multiple clinical institutions.

title: Early In-ovo Sexing of Mojosari Duck Eggs on Day 5 Using Hybrid Feature Fusion and Machine Learning
abstract: Early in-ovo sexing can support more efficient hatchery management by enabling sex determination before hatching.This study investigates a non-invasive framework for sexing Mojosari duck eggs at day 5 by integrating external morphological, embryonic vascular, and Gray-Level Co-occurrence Matrix (GLCM)-based textural features.External morphological measurements, including egg length and width, were obtained directly using a digital caliper, while egg weight was measured using a digital weighing scale; embryonic vascular and textural features were extracted from RGB candling images acquired with the eggshell intact.A total of 503 labeled eggs were analyzed.Statistical differences between female and male eggs were assessed using Welch's t-test with Holm adjustment and Hedges' g effect sizes, showing significant differences in Length, Width, Weight, and Sinus Terminalis Area.Four classifiers Logistic Regression, Random Forest, SVM-RBF, and XGBoost, were evaluated using Bayesian optimization and stratified cross-validation, with model configuration determined exclusively from training and validation data.On the independent test set of 100 eggs, Random Forest achieved 85.00% accuracy, 82.16% balanced accuracy, 83.41% Macro-F1, and 0.9285 ROC-AUC.Batch-held-out evaluation yielded 80.44% accuracy, 75.92% balanced accuracy, 77.22% Macro-F1, and 0.8795 ROC-AUC.The study provides application-level evidence for day-5 in-ovo sexing of Mojosari duck eggs using low-cost RGB candling, while characterizing sex-related features and contribution of feature groups (hybrid feature fusion).Future studies should validate the approach across broader duck populations, incubation stages, and imaging conditions.

title: Markhor Optimization Algorithm: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm for Solving Optimization Problems
abstract: This study aims to develop a new nature-inspired metaheuristic optimization algorithm called the Markhor Optimization Algorithm (MOA).The core concept of MOA is derived from the natural behaviors of the Markhor in rugged, rocky, and mountainous terrains.In this approach, predator-aware escape behavior and movement toward more suitable terrain guide exploration and global search, while the security-conscious use of suitable habitats and localized movements form the basis for exploitation and local refinement.These behaviors are translated into mathematical rules-serving as a computational abstraction-to simultaneously manage search space coverage and the gradual improvement of solutions.To evaluate the proposed method's performance, a simulation study is conducted using 23 standard benchmark functions, comprising unimodal test functions (F1-F7), high-dimensional multimodal test functions (F8-F13), and fixed-dimensional multimodal test functions (F14-F23).MOA is compared against nine other metaheuristic optimization algorithms across 20 independent runs and 1,000 iterations; performance is assessed using mean, standard deviation (std), rank, and convergence curves.The study's findings demonstrate that MOA delivers stable and highly competitive performance across all three categories of benchmark functions, achieving a rank of 1 for all 23 functions.Consequently, optimization analyses reveal that MOA-by securing the top rank in every benchmark function-acts as the best-performing optimizer with a 100% success rate, demonstrating superior competitiveness against rival algorithms.These results indicate that the design of MOA, leveraging two complementary Markhor behaviors, provides an effective framework for simultaneously managing exploration and exploitation in various optimization problems.

title: YourPose-CNN: A Multi-Head Mask-Guided Unified Framework for Head Pose Estimation Using ZetaLite U-Net
abstract: The research work indicated here involves the development of unified framework which is capable of performing both discrete as well as continuous head pose estimation.In the first stage the face is detected through Sample and Computation Redistribution for Face Detection (SCRFD).In the second stage the Nose-Lip region mask is constructed for detected face through ZetaLite U-net model, a memory efficient and powerful U-net designed for efficient Nose-Lip mask extraction.In the third stage YourPose-CNN(a multi task multi head CNN) is designed which concatenates the detected face with the nose-lip mask for estimating the Euler angles as well head pose class among seven classes considered in this research study.On the BIWI dataset, ZetaLite U-Net attained higher training and validation accuracy than the conventional U-Net (99.01%vs. 96.40%and 98.29% vs. 93.80%)and a comparable validation IoU (87.48% vs 87.56%), while using far fewer parameters.The proposed model achieves an overall MAE of 4.0671° for regression and a classification accuracy of 94.84% on the BIWI test dataset, where the training validation and testing partitions are completely subject disjoint.Its potential for use in a variety of video analytics applications is further demonstrated by the cross-domain evaluation carried out on various image and video-based datasets, as detailed in this study.

title: Evaluation Protocol Matters More Than Model Choice: A Simulated-data Study of Intrusion Detection from Raw Network Metadata Under a Preserved Class Prior
abstract: Intrusion detection systems must defend enterprise and IoT networks against increasingly sophisticated threats.We evaluate five machine learning classifiers on 10,000 network flow records covering nine attack categories and a benign class, using 26 features engineered from 13 raw metadata attributes.Departing from common practice, we partition before balancing, so the held-out set of 3,000 flows retains the 24 to 1 class ratio of the source data; hyperparameters are tuned on the training partition alone and standardisation is fitted inside a leakage-free pipeline.Gradient boosting attains the highest area under the precision-recall curve (0.670), detecting 66.67% of attacks at a 1.28% false-positive rate, with random forest close behind (0.659).Evaluation protocol dominates model choice: logistic regression appears competitive on a balanced partition, yet its attack-class precision falls to 13.91% at the 4% prevalence of the source data.Binary detection is viable from raw metadata; fine-grained attribution is not.Because all results come from one simulated distribution whose generator is unavailable to us, they characterise that distribution rather than deployed intrusion detection, and the feature rankings describe the fitted models rather than establishing that the underlying fields are intrinsically diagnostic of attacks.A prevalence-sensitivity analysis shows how precision degrades at the lower priors typical of production traffic.

title: Decoupling Contamination Detection from Classification Accuracy: A Confidence-based Triage Framework with Explainable AI for Water Quality Monitoring
abstract: Binary classification is the standard approach in machine learning-based water quality monitoring, but its false negative rates remain a practical concern-contaminated samples misclassified as safe go undetected.This study applies selective prediction to water potability screening and characterises the resulting Accuracy-Safety Decoupling, demonstrating that contamination detection can be substantially improved independently of overall classification accuracy through a confidence-based triage framework.Rather than relying on binary decision boundaries, the framework sorts predictions into safe, uncertain, and contaminated zones using dual probability thresholds, directing uncertain cases to human review instead of automatic clearance.A Random Forest classifier was trained on 46 features engineered from 15 physicochemical parameters in a synthetic water quality dataset of 2,500 samples generated under controlled conditions to isolate framework performance from dataset-specific artifacts.The model achieved 79.2% accuracy and 86.79% ROC-AUC.The triage system raised the contamination capture rate from 75.21% to 98.3%, a triage-level measure of samples not auto-cleared as safe, an improvement confirmed by McNemar's test (χ² = 26.04,p < 0.0001), A paired risk difference of 23.14 percentage points (95% CI [15.63, 30.65]), and non-overlapping bootstrap confidence intervals.SHAP and LIME analysis showed moderate-to-strong agreement (Spearman ρ = 0.608), with chloramines, turbidity, and pH emerging as the top predictive factors.The dataset was generated under a documented parametric specification with an explicit rule-based labelling function, establishing a controlled methodological baseline against which future real-world deployments can be benchmarked.

title: Trustworthy Explainable Artificial Intelligence for Comprehensive Alzheimer's Disease Diagnosis, Staging, and Progression Prediction Using Multimodal Data
abstract: Alzheimer's Disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative condition and requires a suitable diagnosis followed by accurate staging and reliable prediction of disease progression, along with continuous decision support to manage patients effectively.It is obvious that despite the fact that existing approaches utilizing artificial intelligence (AI) technologies have shown great promise in terms of diagnostic capabilities, they are more focused on isolated problems, use only unimodal data, and lack proper explanation capabilities and reliability, which creates a serious hindrance to their applying to the clinical practice.Thus, in order to solve these existing issues, the authors of the article present the concept of a Trustworthy Explainable Artificial Intelligence (TXAI) framework based on multimodal data, which can provide comprehensive diagnostic capabilities for Alzheimer's Disease, its staging, progression prediction, and clinical decision support.The TXAI framework utilizes various input data, particularly structural MRI, PET scans, specific cognitive tests (MMSE, CDR, and ADAS-Cog), demographic data, and important biomarkers connected to particular patients.In relation to the issue of trustworthiness, the authors mention that the TXAI framework includes methods of uncertainty estimation, model calibration, reliability evaluation, and techniques of explainable AI that allow providing accurate predictions accompanied by explanations valid in clinical practice.In addition to that, it is worth mentioning that the TXAI framework deals with disease stage estimation, predictions of progression risk, and calculation of the risk score at the same time.The framework was evaluated using publicly available Alzheimer's Disease datasets, including ADNI, OASIS, and AIBL, under patient-independent stratified cross-validation.Comparative experiments with conventional and deep-learning baselines demonstrate the effectiveness of TXAI for multimodal diagnosis and disease staging, while additional analyses assess progression, trustworthiness, explainability, robustness, and personalized risk assessment.

title: Integrated Centrifugal Pump Design Using 3D Modelling, Digital Twins, and Additive Prototyping
abstract: Centrifugal pump development still moves through separate islands of information: a one-dimensional sizing calculation, a manually built solid model, a physical prototype, and a drawing package produced after the geometry is frozen.This paper proposes and tests a design technology in which parametric 3D geometry, multi-fidelity CFD, a reduced-order digital twin, additively manufactured prototypes and machine-readable documentation are all views of one versioned design record.Thirty-four continuous variables plus one discrete blade number Z (35 optimisation variables in total) control the meridional channel and the blade loading, with manufacturability enforced inside the generator; a co-Kriging surrogate coupling coarse steady and fine transient cavitating simulations drives an NSGA-III search; a POD-Galerkin model corrected by an unscented Kalman filter forms the operational twin; and the sensitivity matrix produced by the optimiser is reused to allocate manufacturing tolerances.The framework was applied to three pumps of different duty (Case A, nq = 37.0; Case B, nq = 12.7; Case C, nq = 32.3;recalculated from Eq. ( 1) with Q in m³ s⁻¹) and validated against ISO 9906 Grade 1B tests.Three results are central.First, the two-level surrogate reached the same Pareto front quality as single-fidelity Kriging with 4.2 times fewer high-fidelity simulations, and measured best-point efficiency rose by 2.9-4.7 percentage points.Second, an equivalent-sand-roughness correction brought as-built selective laser melted prototypes to within 0.9 percentage points of cast production efficiency, against an uncorrected deficit of about 5 points, which turns a printed impeller into a quantitative performance predictor rather than a form-and-fit check.Third, in a two-unit field study over 4300 h the twin tracked head to 1.2 % mean absolute error and estimated wear-ring clearance to within 0.03 mm of the post-overhaul measurement.Design-cycle and documentation metrics from 14 releases are reported as associations rather than causal effects, since the comparison was not randomised.

title: A Comparative Evaluation of Selective FP32 and INT8 Poultry Fecal-image Classifiers under Classwise Risk Screening
abstract: A selective classifier can assign a label or defer an uncertain poultry fecal image.We evaluated MobileNetV2 and EfficientNetB0 using 7,695 images retained from an 8,067-image archive after duplicate and labelconflict screening.Both backbones were trained with three seeds and exported in FP32 and INT8.Validation selected 24 abstention rules; a separate calibration partition screened their classwise automatic-error risk against a ten percent target.Seven MobileNetV2 rules passed; 17 failed the Newcastle bound and were assigned all-defer.On 1,154 heldout test images, the passing rules labelled 68.46 to 76.52 percent automatically.Class-specific thresholds did not improve coverage in either matched setting where both rule types passed.INT8 reduced model size but did not consistently improve host CPU latency.The small Newcastle calibration stratum limited certification despite strong conventional classification scores.Post-hoc sensitivity analyses indicated that Newcastle calibration size and multiplicity accounting, rather than raw accuracy, largely determined certification.

title: SHAP-initialised Binary Grey Wolf Optimisation for Feature Selection in Network Intrusion Detection: When Importance-Proportional Seeding Fails
abstract: Network intrusion detection relies on feature selection to control dimensionality across severely imbalanced traffic classes, and metaheuristic wrappers such as the grey wolf optimiser dominate this literature.Seeding such a search with feature importance rather than at random is an attractive refinement, and informed initialisation is well supported elsewhere; that literature also warns that importance seeding which ignores subset size and inter-feature redundancy is its principal failure mode, and this has not been quantified for intrusion detection.We implement SHAPinitialised binary grey wolf optimisation (SHAP-BGWO), drawing each initial mask as xj ∼ Bernoulli(φj/maxk φk) from mean absolute SHAP values, and evaluate a 2 × 2 ablation separating the warm start from a SHAP-coherence fitness term against a no-selection control, five conventional selectors and the reimplemented selection stages of two recent methods, on CIC-IDS2017 and UNSW-NB15 over 10 seeds with an audited train/test firewall, BCa intervals and Holm correction.Maximum normalisation collapses the expected initial subset to 8.1 of 78 features on CIC-IDS2017 and 4.9 of 42 on UNSW-NB15.On CIC-IDS2017, SHAP seeding changes macro-F1 by -18.67 points without the coherence term and by -11.25 points with it; neither contrast is significant at ten seeds, and no arm reaches Boruta (0.8000) or the no-selection control (0.7767) in mean macro-F1.On UNSW-NB15 the two contrasts are -11.56 and -12.49points and both are significant after Holm correction.A corrected re-run that selects the ensemble's class leaders on a training-side calibration split, under a prior that collapses the initial subset far less (21.1 of 78 and 13.5 of 42 features), shows no comparable loss, which locates the failure in the collapse of the initial subset rather than in importance seeding as such.Importance-proportional seeding needs an explicit size or redundancy constraint to be viable.

title: A Blockchain-based Decentralized Deep Matrix Factorization Recommender System
abstract: Recommender systems are widely used to support personalized item discovery; however, conventional centralized architectures still raise important concerns related to privacy exposure, reliance on a central authority, limited verifiability, data manipulation risks, and single-point-of-failure limitations.To address these issues, this research proposes a privacy-aware, blockchain-supported decentralized recommendation framework with off-chain recommendation computation and blockchain-based authorization and integrity verification, connecting Decentralized Communities-Deep Matrix Factorization (DC-DMF) with trusted authorized node selection, smart-contract-based announcement and finalization, and hash-based recommendation-delivery verification.The framework uses previously detected interest communities as the structural basis for community-aware recommendation computation.For each interest community, a trusted authorized node Ak is selected off-chain using social-relationship evidence from the social graph and then announced, confirmed, and finalized through a smart contract.Model training, recommendation ranking, and user-specific recommendation-package preparation are performed off-chain, while blockchain is used for authorization checks, compact hash-record storage, and delivery-integrity verification.The proposed framework was evaluated using the Douban Movie and Last.fm datasets under DMF-Whole network, CC-DMF, and DC-DMF recommendation scenarios.The results show that the voting stage was evaluated under different levels of available social-relationship evidence.Douban Movie provided limited social-relationship evidence, whereas Last.fm provided wider social-relationship evidence; however, both datasets produced finalized Ak values through the blockchain-based announcement and confirmation process.In Last.fm,DC-DMF mean Recall increased from 0.2915 at K=50 to 0.5588 at K=300, while CC-DMF mean Recall increased from 0.3473 to 0.6254.In Douban Movie, DC-DMF reported mean F1 values of 0.3129 and 0.3563 at K=10 and K=20, respectively, while CC-DMF reported mean F1 values of 0.2168 and 0.2267.In the recommendation-delivery stage, the stored delivery hashes matched the recomputed hashes of the corresponding off-chain recommendation packages, and the modification check showed that changing one recommended item in a representative package from each dataset resulted in a hash mismatch and rejection during verification.Overall, the results show that DC-DMF recommendation computation, blockchain-based community authorization, and hash-based delivery-integrity checking were integrated within the proposed on-chain/off-chain framework.

title: DTW-RL: Adaptive Routing Evaluation Interval Algorithm for Stable and Reliable RPL in Mobile IoT Networks
abstract: Routing stability remains a critical challenge in the IPv6 Routing Protocol for Low-Power and Lossy Networks (RPL), particularly in dynamic Internet of Things (IoT) environments characterized by mobility, fluctuating link qualities, and frequent topology changes.Although multi-metric routing approaches have improved parent selection decisions, most existing schemes continue to perform routing evaluations at fixed intervals, which may introduce unnecessary overhead during stable periods or delay their adaptation under dynamic conditions.This study presents and evaluates a complete DTW-RL configuration that integrates MMDEW based parent selection with adaptive routing evaluation interval control through an algorithmically compact linear Q-learning mechanism.The algorithm was implemented in Contiki-NG and evaluated using the Cooja simulator under mobility scenarios involving two to five mobile nodes.Performance was compared against the Minimum Rank with Hysteresis Objective Function (MRHOF) and MMDEW using Packet Delivery Ratio (PDR), handover count (HO), End-to-End Delay, and Energy Consumption metrics.The experimental results indicate fewer recorded preferred parent changes and improved communication reliability for the evaluated DTW-RL configuration.Under the five mobile node changing trajectory scenario at the 20 s transmission interval, DTW-RL reduced handover events by 97.72% compared with MRHOF and 47.66% compared with MMDEW.Its PDR were 71.28%, 97.37%, and 97.97% at transmission intervals of 10, 20, and 30 s, respectively.Furthermore, DTW-RL achieved the lowest end-to-end delay at transmission intervals of 10 s and 20 s in the five-mobile node scenario, whereas its higher delay in the two-mobile node scenario indicates a trade-off between routing stability and latency.Exploratory paired tests using six matched condition means found fewer handovers for DTW-RL than for MRHOF and MMDEW after Holm adjustment across eight comparisons (adjusted p = 0.0338 for each comparison).Under the evaluated conditions, the complete DTW-RL configuration demonstrated a trade-off between routing stability, communication reliability, and resource utilization.

title: A Graph Neural Network Approach for Joint Security and Performance Management
abstract: The dilemma in today's cloud data centers is how to maximize resources and optimize network performance in the face of this rapidly expanding attack surface of denial of service, lateral movement and anomalous resource exploitation.Typical optimization techniques, such as heuristic schedulers and queue-based load balancers, or individual machine learning predictors, are generally addressing these objectives individually, and are not delivering optimal solutions or timely threat response.To cope with these challenges, the paper proposes a novel intelligent framework SecOpt-GNN that incorporates the cloud network performance optimization and anomaly detection for security.The performance optimization head makes task placement and routing decisions and the security head is real-time anomaly and intrusion scoring.A Graph Attention Network (GAT) based encoder is learned to provide two collaborating heads with joint representations: one head generates task placements and routing decisions, the other head scores real-time anomalies and intrusions.The framework is trained and tested with a real-world Google cluster trace data.Experimental results show that SecOpt-GNN obtains 96.4% accuracy for anomaly detection, averaged as the mean of the per-load percentage reductions across the six load levels, SecOpt-GNN reduces scheduling latency by 37.8% relative to round-robin (equivalently, a 45.1% reduction in mean latency, from 42.2 ms to 23.2 ms; per-load reductions range 16.7%-52.2%),and better results than the standard GCN, GraphSAGE, LSTM, ContrastNet, and Random Forest baselines on all scoring metrics.The results indicate that the current methods that optimize for the security or performance objectives of each network separately are sub-optimal when considering a holistic view of security and performance objectives via joint graph-based modelling.

title: Bimodal Pareto Structure in Metaheuristic Tuning of Fractional-order PI Control for A DC Microgrid: An Inverted Oustaloup Realisation and A Threshold-defined Settling-time Objective
abstract: Direct-current microgrids concentrate photovoltaic, wind and battery conversion behind one lightly buffered bus, and fractional-order PI control is widely used to regulate it.Since s -λ is irrational, every such controller is a rational approximation of one.We tune a dual-loop fractional-order PI regulator for a 48 V bus with four multi-objective metaheuristics against steady-state accuracy and settling time, and examine the bimodal Pareto front that results.In the published implementation, the Oustaloup block assigns zeros and poles to a differentiator's grids while carrying an integrator's gain constant, so integral action is absent; the bus parks at the edge of the settling band and the slow cluster is produced by millivolt threshold grazes: 91 % of its points leave the band by less than 5 mV, and a 24 mV change of the band moves 85 % of the front.Correcting the realisation reduces the dip statistic by a factor of 3.1 (hierarchical-bootstrap 95 % CI 2.4-4.0,120 independent runs); the residual two-cluster structure is physical rather than threshold-induced and disappears under tuning on randomised scenarios.Only 3.9 % of the original search box is linearly stable; restricting the search to it removes saturation-driven limit cycles without loss of held-out accuracy.On 150 held-out scenarios, the corrected controller with adequate integral-gain bounds achieves a median IAE of 0.0087 V s, against 0.0146 V s for reconstructed fractional-order sliding-mode and active-disturbance-rejection controllers.All raw results and code are released.

title: MADSCAG: A Missingness-aware Early Warning System for Village-level Rice Pest Surveillance Under Reactive Monitoring
abstract: Rice pest patrols go where farmers report trouble, so the register measures the observer as much as the pest.A forecast fitted to it inherits that bias.Is the observation process better modelled than corrected away?MADSCAG, missingness-aware decoupled stages for capacity allocation and guidance, predicts attendance and conditional severity separately on an East Java register of 114,757 village-periods, scored once chronologically.After a gap, officers found an attack 87.1% of the time against 43.1%; attendance reaches AUC 0.789 against 0.662 for a visit-rate rule; intervals cover 90.0 to 90.5% marginally, 2.1% on the largest outbreaks; the better-ranked half of visited villages holds 64.9% of recorded severity, 30% above random.No accuracy advantage over a recurrent alternative is demonstrated.Reactive registers make the visit predictable and informative, but no decision product built on it beat simpler rules, the blindspot list included; validating missed outbreaks needs prospective sampling.

title: AgentShield Hybrid Runtime Firewall Architecture for Secure Tool Governance in Agentic Large Language Model Systems
abstract: The Agentic large language model (LLM) systems introduce a critical security boundary in which modelgenerated reasoning can trigger consequential external tool actions.This paper presents AgentShield-FW, a hybrid runtime firewall that separates reasoning from execution authority through typed Action Intent Objects, deterministic policy enforcement, classifier-assisted risk assessment, verifier-based route correction, approval and sandbox controls, and tamper-evident auditing.Evaluation combined a 20,000-case deterministic AAF-Bench generator, a leakagecontrolled public corpus, authorization-specific governance tests, adaptive adversarial evaluation, and interactive AgentDojo execution.From 56,155 normalized public records, exact-content deduplication retained 26,129 Clean V2 samples, including a held-out test set of 2,613 cases.On this set, AgentShield-FW achieved 1.77% attack success rate, 98.23% attack blocking, 98.16% F1, 95.29% balanced accuracy, and 97.05% safe completion.A bounded white-box adaptive evaluation produced 0/310 successful malicious trajectories under the specified mutation budget.On the official AgentDojo v1.2.2 subset, injection-task success decreased from 33.33% without protection to 0%, and unsafe canonical tool execution decreased from 92.86% to 0%.However, benign task success decreased from 58.33% to 16.67%, revealing substantial over-blocking.Verifier-specific analysis similarly showed improved malicious containment but measurable benign escalation and route-correctness degradation.The results demonstrate that actionlevel runtime mediation can strongly constrain unsafe agent behaviour while preserving reproducible governance evidence, but they also identify a significant security-utility trade-off that must be addressed before utility-preserving production deployment.

title: Separating Probability Calibration from Selective Reliability in Transformer-based Stress Detection under Domain Shift
abstract: Probability calibration does not establish selective reliability in stress detection.This study jointly audits calibration, selective prediction, training variability, domain shift, and semantic stability on Dreaddit, controlling data leakage and accounting for post clustering.BERT, RoBERTa, and DeBERTa are evaluated across five paired training seeds using temperature scaling and label smoothing of strength 0.10, yielding 30 fits and 45 evaluation conditions.Both interventions reduce Brier score, negative log likelihood, and expected calibration error in every backbone and seed pair.Temperature scaling preserves F1 and area under the risk coverage curve in all 15 pairs.Label smoothing increases this area for RoBERTa across all seeds, while BERT and DeBERTa vary in direction.Archived domain holdout and topic stability analyses provide diagnostics conditional on fitted models.This integrated audit distinguishes findings consistent across retraining from conclusions conditional on fitted models, separating training variability from clustered test uncertainty.Generalization remains limited to Dreaddit.

title: AURA-CXR: Development-locked Hybrid CNN–ViT and Adaptive Radiomics Stacking with Quantitative XAI for Pneumonia Detection
abstract: Pneumonia detection on chest X-rays is difficult because findings are subtle and images vary across datasets.Combining representations can help, but components must be selected without reusing test data.AURA-CXR stacks a convolutional network (DenseNet121-XRV), a Vision Transformer (EVA-X-S), and entropy-guided Adaptive Radiomics via Logistic Regression.Of 26,684 RSNA patientIds, 21,346 formed the development cohort and 5,338 the locked test.Every component, coefficient, and threshold was fixed from out-of-fold development predictions before testing.The frozen stack reached a locked-test ROC-AUC of 0.8988, above either encoder alone and slightly above a same-split ConvNeXt V2 Tiny baseline (0.8922; 0.8960 in an initial run).Without adaptation, it achieved 0.9309 on the pediatric Kermany cohort.Ablations attributed the RSNA gain to combining both encoders, not to radiomics or adaptive wavelet selection.Deep-branch attribution maps localized better than simple spatial priors but were methoddependent.AURA-CXR offers a selection-locked, reproducible protocol measuring each component's contribution.

title: ECG-based Identification of Ischemic Patterns Associated with Coronary Artery Disease Using a Hybrid Temporal Fusion Transformer-TabNet Framework on 12-lead ECG Signals
abstract: Coronary artery disease (CAD) is still the primary cause of cardiovascular mortality in the world.Accurate automated detection systems are essential.In this paper, a novel hybrid deep learning framework is proposed whose primary novelty lies not in the TFT or TabNet architectures individually; both of them are established in their respective domains.This paper focuses on their systematic integration and joint optimisation for multimodal ECG-based identification of ischemic ECG patterns associated with CAD from 12-lead ECG signals and structured clinical metadata.The experiments were performed on the largest public annotated ECG database (PTB-XL).The PTB-XL dataset was not originally assembled as a dedicated ischemic-pattern repository.PTB-XL includes structured SCP-ECG diagnostic annotations, from which ischemic and infarction-related ECG phenotypes associated with CAD can be systematically identified.This paper provides a rigorous, clinically justified derivation of Ischemic-positive and Ischemic-negative labels from PTB-XL and then constructs a 21,837-record binary classification benchmark.The proposed framework is validated using a 5-fold stratified cross-validation method on a training set consisting of 17776 samples, with a mean validation accuracy of 0.9500.Importantly, PTB-XL's labels come from SCP-ECG diagnostic annotations, not angiography-confirmed coronary artery disease diagnoses.This study therefore focuses on identifying ischemic ECG patterns associated with CAD, rather than making a direct clinical CAD diagnosis.

title: NRGA-Net: Noise-residual Guided Attention Network for Local Manipulation Detection and Localization in Satellite Imagery
abstract: Modern satellite imagery has become vulnerable to numerous manipulation threats due to the rapid progress of generative models, and forensic analysis is important to detect malicious edits and to secure the critical decisions that rely on remote-sensing data.Though, the purpose of this study is driven by the security issues that can be witnessed in satellite-based decision making, the presented framework is tested as a unified forgery localization and detection system with a reference to the benchmark forgery datasets.The suggested model combines a dilated DenseNet-201 semantic encoder with a dual-domain forensic lane that fuses a fixed-filter noise-residual stream and a learnable frequency-residual encoder through asymmetric cross-frequency attention, while a spectral-edge stream recovers boundaries in the Fourier domain, and the new Fake-LocalDiff benchmark adds prompt-driven latent-diffusion local replacements to the existing inpainting benchmarks.The proposed model is implemented and evaluated as a supervised forgery detector using labeled data, and it is evaluated on Fake-Vaihingen, Fake-LoveDA, and Fake-LocalDiff under an immutable train, calibration, and final-test protocol to analyze its effectiveness in localizing forged and authentic regions and in detecting manipulated images.Because each generative model imprints its own characteristics, features, and fingerprint on the forged images, the model is trained jointly on the three datasets (LaMa inpainting, RePaint, and latent diffusion), and the leave-one-family-out study shows that omitting one family from training weakens the model and prevents it from capturing the artifacts of the unseen generator.The performance on the independent final-test set is astounding, with a 97.80% pooled forged-class IoU, a Dice = F1 of 98.89%, a precision of 98.31%, a recall of 99.48%, and a 99.22% detection accuracy.The applicability of the proposed model to multispectral imagery and to unseen generator families is considered indicative, and future work will focus on contrastive validation of the provenance hash and on improving cross-generator transfer.The experimental analysis is done based on the three benchmarks, albeit under the incentive of the satellite-imagery security issues, thus the findings provide insights into the performance of the unified supervised framework on the benchmark protocols.

title: A Graph-enhanced Multimodal Transformer Framework for Continuous Sign Language Recognition and Gloss-assisted Translation
abstract: Continuous sign language translation (CSLT) aims to convert continuous signing into spoken-language text, but fixed multimodal fusion may fail to adapt to changing visual cues.We propose a graph-enhanced multimodal Transformer using gloss-assisted training with gloss-free inference.The framework combines RGB appearance, skeletal pose, and facial landmarks through adaptive cross-modal weighting and a temporal saliency gate.A CTCbased recognition objective and an autoregressive translation objective are jointly optimized during training, while gloss prediction is not required during inference.On PHOENIX-2014T, the model achieved 17.80 ± 0.20% WER, 25.40 ± 0.12 BLEU-4, and 34.80 ± 0.15 ROUGE-L.On CSL-Daily, it improved BLEU-4 by 0.70 over the strongest baseline.The framework achieved 22 FPS inference throughput under the reported configuration, while ablation and robustness experiments indicated contributions from multimodal fusion and resilience to degraded inputs.

title: Attainable-performance Bounds from Label Conflict in Multiclass Network Intrusion Detection: A Controlled Evaluation on UNSW-NB15
abstract: Reported multiclass accuracies for machine-learning intrusion detection on UNSW-NB15 range from roughly 61% to 88%, a spread far wider than any plausible difference between algorithms.This paper separates what the corpus permits from what models achieve.On the official train-to-test partition (175,341 / 82,332 flows), five model families (Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost and a hybrid Transformer-Kolmogorov-Arnold Network) are trained under one protocol, with validation-only model selection and five-seed replication.From label conflict among identical feature vectors we derive exact upper bounds that hold for every deterministic classifier on the input each family receives.Label conflict caps per-class F1 at 0.262 for Analysis, 0.271 for Backdoor and 0.679 for DoS; the jointly attainable macro-F1, computed exactly by mixed-integer programming, is 0.785, and the accuracy bound, 93.60%, equals one minus the empirical Bayes error of the test sample.Per-class recall ceilings, by contrast, depend on the objective and differ by a factor of 8.8 for Backdoor.Exact-duplicate conflict accounts for at most 27.7% of the best model's accuracy error and 45.8% of its macro-F1 shortfall.The five families reach 47.5% to 53.0% macro-F1, with Random Forest leading (53.02 ± 0.17), and their errors overlap strongly: 16.1% of test rows are misclassified by all five, against 0.09% expected under independence, and most of these common errors are not forced by label conflict.Five-seed single-factor controls show that a KAN head is indistinguishable from a parameter-matched MLP head, while class balancing lowers accuracy and raises balanced accuracy in every family, tree ensembles included.A random pooled split raises XGBoost accuracy by 6.6 points, but duplicated test rows are classified less accurately than unduplicated ones, so the gain is not memorisation and is best explained by a within-class distribution shift between the official partitions.Applied unchanged to CICIDS2017, the procedure gives an accuracy bound of 99.985%, showing that the severity of label conflict is specific to UNSW-NB15.We recommend reporting per-class ceilings alongside per-class scores.

title: A Lightweight Depthwise CNN with Efficient Attention Optimized by Chinese Pangolin Algorithm for Accurate and Low-latency IoMT intrusion Detection
abstract: The rapid adoption of Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) technologies has improved healthcare monitoring, diagnosis, and patient management while simultaneously increasing exposure to diverse cyber threats.This study proposes a Chinese Pangolin Optimization-based Lightweight Depthwise Convolutional Neural Network with Efficient Attention (CPOA-LDCNN-EA) for accurate and computationally efficient IoMT intrusion detection.The framework integrates depthwise separable convolution for lightweight feature extraction, Efficient Attention for discriminative feature enhancement, and Chinese Pangolin Optimization for joint feature-retention evaluation and hyperparameter optimization.CICIoMT2024 was employed as the source dataset for model development and internal evaluation, whereas ToN-IoT and CICIDS2017 were used exclusively as unseen target datasets for external crossdataset evaluation.On CICIoMT2024, the proposed framework achieved a five-run mean accuracy of 99.41 ± 0.18%, Macro-Precision of 99.27 ± 0.20%, Macro-Recall of 99.18 ± 0.23%, Macro-F1 of 99.22 ± 0.21%, and Macro PR-AUC of 0.9966 ± 0.0011.The representative median-performance run achieved approximately 99.40% Macro-Precision, 99.40% Macro-Recall, and 99.40% Macro-F1, with a Macro one-vs-rest ROC-AUC of 0.998 and a Macro PR-AUC of 0.997.Without target-domain retraining or optimization, the frozen source-trained model achieved accuracies of 98.87% on ToN-IoT and 98.54% on CICIDS2017, demonstrating high binary cross-dataset transfer accuracy under the adopted Benign/Attack harmonization protocol.The framework contains 3.2 million trainable parameters and requires 1.4 GFLOPs, with a model-forward latency of 1.58 ms/sample on an NVIDIA RTX 3080 GPU.Samecondition comparisons on CICIoMT2024 indicate a favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-off relative to the evaluated baselines.These findings demonstrate the potential of CPOA-LDCNN-EA for edge-assisted IoMT cybersecurity, while further evaluation on resource-constrained healthcare devices is required to establish direct on-device deployment performance.

title: MVST: A Multi-view Spatio-temporal Transformer for Skill-aware Tennis Stroke Recognition from Skeleton Sequences
abstract: This paper proposes a Multi-View Spatio-Temporal Transformer (MVST) for skill-aware tennis stroke recognition from paired skeleton sequences.Estimating a player's skill level from movement patterns, beyond recognizing the performed action itself, remains a challenging problem in computer vision.A shared transformer encoder models spatial landmark relationships and temporal motion dynamics, while back-view and side-view representations are fused to reduce viewpoint ambiguity.A Cross-View Alignment (CVA) objective is introduced as an auxiliary contrastive loss that aligns view-level embeddings of the same stroke instance during training, with no inference overhead.On a self-collected dataset of eight subjects and 96 paired stroke instances, evaluated under a reproducible five-seed, four-fold subject-independent protocol, MVST with CVA achieves a final-epoch accuracy of 0.83, showing higher mean accuracy than ST-GCN, SkateFormer and SA-TDGFormer while achieving comparable performance to CTR-GCN with 2.4 times fewer parameters and 1.4 times fewer FLOPs.A leave-one-subject-out analysis achieves 0.85 skill-classification accuracy on subjects excluded from training, indicating that the learned representation can generalize to unseen subjects within this cohort.

title: EfficientNet–Fuzzy ShCNN Framework for Multi-class Cotton Leaf Disease Classification Using Adaptive Feature Fusion
abstract: The early and accurate recognition of cotton leaf diseases is important for improving crop productivity and supporting precision agriculture.This study proposes an EfficientNet-Fuzzy ShCNN architecture for multi-class cotton leaf disease classification under complex imaging conditions.The proposed framework integrates EfficientNetbased deep feature extraction, a long-range attention mechanism, adaptive fuzzy feature weighting, and a lightweight depthwise ShCNN classifier to improve classification performance and robustness.The model was evaluated using a publicly available Kaggle Cotton Leaf Disease dataset containing four classes: Healthy, Bacterial Blight, Leaf Curl Virus, and Fusarium Wilt.Following dataset screening and experimental-subset construction, 1,400 original images were retained and stratified into training, validation, and independent test subsets prior to augmentation.Data augmentation was applied exclusively to the training subset to prevent information leakage.Experimental results show that the proposed framework achieves a classification accuracy of 98.72%, with precision, recall, and F1-score values exceeding 98% and an error rate of 1.28%.The framework also demonstrates computational efficiency with 4.87 million trainable parameters, 0.46 GFLOPs, and an average neural-network inference time of 3.79 ms per image, indicating low inference latency under the evaluated GPU environment.Comparative evaluation demonstrates that the proposed framework provides a favorable balance between classification performance and computational complexity relative to the evaluated baseline and recent deep-learning architectures.Component-wise ablation analysis further demonstrates the contribution of the preprocessing, attention, fuzzy weighting, feature-fusion, ShCNN, and optimization stages.A Friedman repeated-measures analysis across the matched training seeds identified an overall difference among the evaluated architectures (𝜒 𝐹 2, (4) = 20.00𝑝 ≈ 0.00050).Exact paired Wilcoxon signed-rank post-hoc tests with Holm correction were additionally performed; however, the individual pairwise comparisons did not reach the conventional 0.05 significance level because only five matched runs were available.

title: PDC-Mask R-CNN: Pixel Difference Convolution for Enhanced Instance Segmentation of Multi-label Oral Lesions in Intraoral RGB Images
abstract: Oral lesions in intraoral RGB images are small with indistinct boundaries, complicating segmentation.We propose PDC-Mask R-CNN, a multi-label instance segmentation framework that embeds Pixel Difference Convolution (PDC) into selected ResNet-50 residual blocks while leaving the prediction pipeline unchanged.PDC models interpixel intensity differences to strengthen boundaries against convolutional smoothing.We used 3,254 intraoral images (10,428 instances) across five categories: Calculus, Caries, Gingivitis, Ulcer, and Oral Cancer.Patient identifiers were unavailable, so we partitioned at the image level with near-duplicate screening, without claiming patient-level separation, and evaluated a screened test subset (303 images, 857 instances) under the COCO protocol.PDC-Mask R-CNN scored above the baseline on 19 of 22 metrics, including all eleven mask measures: mask AP@[0.50:0.95]rose from 16.695% to 19.317% (+2.622 pp, +15.7% relative), mask AP75 by 2.564 pp (+20.0%relative), and box AP by 1.771 pp (+9.7% relative).Three bounding-box metrics declined (large objects, Calculus, Gingivitis).Ablation attributes 0.276 of the 2.622 pp mask AP to the operator alone, raising AP75 but lowering AP50.Under the same protocol, PDC-Mask R-CNN exceeds the strongest of three evaluated one-stage segmenters, YOLO26l-seg, by 4.156 pp mask AP (+27.4% relative).All differences are descriptive single-run results; transformer-based and boundaryaware segmenters were not evaluated.

title: From Internally Validated Physical Parameters to Leakage-safe Machine Learning for Fine-grained Tactical Vehicle Terrain Classification
abstract: Tactical vehicle terrain classification often relies on statistical features extracted from raw multisensor signals, although their relationship with physical vehicle and occupant responses is not always clear.This study develops a leakage-safe machine-learning approach using internally validated physical parameters for fine-grained terrain classification.Eleven features represented vibration and shock, seat-to-body transmissibility, dynamic stability, translational and rotational motion, and segmental mechanical-load response.Data were segmented into five-second windows with 50 percent overlap, producing 930 windows from 92 independent runs.Run identity was preserved throughout nested cross-validation.Five classifiers were evaluated.Gradient Boosting achieved the highest numerical seven-class Macro-F1 of 0.786, followed by Random Forest at 0.758.Leave-one-domain-out analysis showed that removing segmental mechanical-load features produced the largest and most consistent performance loss.Physical-11 also outperformed Conventional-9 and HFW-GB5 across all classifiers.Three-class gains were driven mainly by label aggregation, while stronger chronological grouping reduced the mean Macro-F1 of the corresponding run-level Physical-11 reference from 0.730 under standard Run_ID grouping to 0.652.

title: DMSA-KANet: Improving Breast Cancer Segmentation in Mammography through Deep Supervision Multi-scale Attention and Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks
abstract: Breast cancer segmentation in mammography remains challenging owing to the small lesion size, low contrast, and overlapping fibroglandular tissue.This study proposes the Deep Supervision Multi-Scale Attention Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (DMSA-KANet), a hybrid architecture that combines an EfficientNetB4 encoder with a high-resolution path, a multi-scale attention bottleneck refined sequentially by Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (KAN) layers, a Vision Transformer, and a KAN-based Convolutional Block Attention Module (KAN-CBAM), and a decoder with KAN-gated skip connections and deep supervision.The model was evaluated on the low-energy images of CDD-CESM (650 images, 282 patients) and on the mass subset of CBIS-DDSM (1,592 images, 892 patients) with patientlevel five-fold cross-validation, in which checkpoint and threshold selection used only validation patients drawn from the training folds, and it was compared with baselines retrained under the same folds, loss, augmentation, epoch budget, and selection rules.Under this protocol DMSA-KANet did not outperform the baselines: it achieved a Dice of 43.97 ± 9.11% on CDD-CESM, the lowest of the seven models, compared with 51.02 ± 3.94% for U-Net and 51.50 ± 3.37% for TransUNet, and 39.98 ± 8.40% on CBIS-DDSM (44.93 ± 1.96% with its learning rates re-selected within the training patients of each fold), compared with 46.80 ± 5.86% for U-Net and 51.06 ± 4.26% for TransUNet, with larger variation across folds than any successfully trained baseline.The gap was associated with fold-level over-segmentation failures and unstable decision thresholds.These results describe retrospective technical performance on two public datasets and indicate that the added architectural complexity did not yield more accurate lesion segmentation under patient-level evaluation.The study provides a reproducible patient-level benchmark for CDD-CESM and CBIS-DDSM, with all fold assignments, code, and per-fold results publicly released.

title: ENHANCING THE RESILIENCE OF CULTURAL DESTINATIONS THROUGH AI-BASED IMMERSIVE EDU-HERITAGE TOURISM: A CASE STUDY OF KASEPUHAN PALACE, CIREBON INDONESIA
abstract: The integration of Artificial Intelligent (AI) and immersive technology has increasingly tranformed how cultural heritage tourism experience. However, existing studies have predominantly focus on technology development or user experience separately understanding of the contribution of AI integration to strengthening the resilience of cultural tourism destinations is still limited. This study aims to examine the role of AI integration in developing edu-heritage tourism experiences and its potential contribution to destination resilience. The research focuses on the implementation of the CAVE LOTUS system at Keraton Kasepuhan Cirebon, Indonesia. The research uses a mixed methods approach with an exploratory sequential design. The qualitative stage is carried out to identify, develop, and validate AI-based historical content that represents important figures and events of the Cirebon Sultanate. The quantitative phase subsequently assessed visitors' perceptions of the immersive experience delivered through the CAVE LOTUS system. The evaluation focused on visual quality, visitor engagement, and the educational value of historical interpretation. The findings indicate an increase in visitor numbers following the implementation of CAVE LOTUS. Visitors also expressed positive perceptions of AI-generated historical visualizations, particularly regarding their ability to present historical figures and narratives in an engaging manner. Furthermore, the immersive experience enhanced visitor engagement and the perceived educational value of cultural heritage interpretation. These findings suggest that integrating AI and immersive technologies can strengthen destination attractiveness by transforming conventional historical interpretation into interactive and educational experiences. Theoretically, this study contributes to edu-heritage tourism literature by connecting AI-driven innovation, immersive visitor experience, and destination resilience within an integrated analytical perspective. Practically, it highlights the potential of AI-enabled immersive technologies to strengthen the adaptive capacity and competitiveness of cultural heritage destinations through digital innovation. Overall, AI integration in edu-heritage tourism represents a promising strategic approach to enhancing destination attractiveness while supporting the long-term resilience of cultural heritage destinations.

title: HYPERMODERN AUTHENTICITY: LUXURY TOURISM IN RAPIDLY CHANGING DESTINATIONS
abstract: The rapid transformation of Riyadh under Saudi Arabia’s Vision 2030 presents luxury travelers with a distinctive challenge: how to understand authenticity in a destination where ambitious modernization and heritage preservation unfold simultaneously. This study examines how luxury tourists interpret authenticity within this evolving environment, focusing on the role of relational service encounters in shaping their experiences and perceptions of luxury. Drawing on an interpretivist, phenomenologically informed approach, the study analyzes 31 semi-structured interviews with high-net-worth luxury tourists who visited Riyadh. Thematic analysis identified three interconnected processes: the recalibration of authenticity, active participation through relational encounters, and the reformulation of luxury meaning. The findings reveal that tourists do not necessarily perceive visible modernization as a threat to cultural authenticity. Instead, meaningful interactions with local residents, tourism guides, and hospitality employees help visitors reconcile contemporary development with cultural heritage and construct more coherent interpretations of the destination. Such encounters enable tourists to move beyond conventional understandings of authenticity based primarily on historical continuity toward interpretations emphasizing cultural sincerity, transparency, and contemporary identity. Moreover, active participation and personalized interactions encourage travelers to redefine luxury beyond material exclusivity and physical comfort, placing greater emphasis on emotional connection, intellectual engagement, and meaningful experiences. Building on these findings, the study introduces the concept of hypermodern authenticity, understood as experiential legitimacy grounded in genuine contemporary cultural commitment expressed through modernization alongside heritage preservation. The study extends tourism authenticity theory by integrating situated meaningmaking and relational value co-creation, while offering practical implications for luxury destination positioning, hospitality service design, and culturally responsive visitor engagement in rapidly transforming destinations.

abstract: The International Conference on Innovation, Sustainability and Digital Transformation in Education, Science, Economics, Medicine, and Artificial Intelligence is an interdisciplinary academic event dedicated to exploring innovative approaches, emerging technologies, sustainable development strategies, and digital transformation across key areas of contemporary society. The conference provides an international platform for researchers, academics, educators, scientists, healthcare professionals, economists, and technology experts to present original research, exchange scientific perspectives, and discuss practical solutions to current global challenges. The main areas of discussion include educational innovation and digital learning, scientific discoveries and technological development, sustainable economic systems, medical innovation and digital healthcare, and the responsible application of artificial intelligence. The conference aims to strengthen interdisciplinary collaboration, promote research excellence, and encourage the development of sustainable, evidence-based solutions through international scientific cooperation.

title: Implementación de la realidad virtual para el entrenamiento de trabajadores en escenarios productivos
abstract: Los accidentes laborales son uno de los mayores problemas de la industria, ya que producen consecuencias tanto en la integridad física, mental y social de los trabajadores, así como en la productividad de las empresas (1). La Organización Internacional del Trabajo (oit) y la Organización Mundial de la Salud (oms), en 2016, evidenciaron que las enfermedades y los traumatismos relacionados con el trabajo provocaron la muerte de 1,9 millones de personas en el mundo (2). En España, durante el año 2022, se registraron 653 510 accidentes de trabajo que generan ausentismo laboral (3). En Colombia, en el 2023, se observó un incremento del 9,3 % en la accidentalidad laboral en comparación con el primer semestre del año anterior (4), alcanzando un total de 542 983 accidentes laborales y registrando un aumento del 6 % con respecto a 2021 (5).

title: Renewable Energy Firms In Transition: Environmental Returns And Policy Synergies Under Saudi Vision 2030
abstract: We examine how renewable energy strategies under Saudi Arabia’s Vision 2030 drive environmental sustainability in fossil fuel-dependent economies. The study analysed data from 42 firms (2012–2023) using the Generalised Method of Moments (GMM) and Impulse Response Functions (IRFs). Our findings indicate that a 1% increase in clean energy investment results in a 6.3–8.1% reduction in climate emissions and a 10.2–16.3% decrease in water challenges. A 1% increase in clean energy use lowers emissions by 5.4–7.6% and water stress by 3.2–11.4%. Policy integration amplifies outcomes. Oil-sector firms leverage scale for renewable projects while non-oil sectors face pressures from oil price volatility. IRFs confirm sustained environmental gains from renewable adoption. The study advocates integrated policies, including subsidy reallocation, lowwater renewables, and oil-sector engagement, to align economic diversification with sustainability. It also emphasises the need to address agricultural water inefficiencies and industrial energy intensity.

title: Comparative Analysis Of Machine Learning Algorithms For Land Use And Land Cover Mapping: Case Study Of Berrechid-Settat Region, Morocco
abstract: This study analyses the spatiotemporal dynamics of Land Use and Land Cover (LULC) in the Berrechid-Settat area of Morocco throughout three reference years: 2010, 2015, and 2023. Satellite images from Landsat 7 (ETM+) and Landsat 8 OLI were processed using the Google Earth Engine (GEE) platform to facilitate quick access, preprocessing, and analysis of extensive datasets. To classify LULC changes and assess the efficacy of machine learning models, Random Forest (RF), Decision Tree (DT), and Support Vector Machine (SVM) were examined. These models were used to categorise five principal LULC classes: water bodies, forests, urban regions, vegetation, and barren lands. Our findings indicated that Random Forest consistently yielded the highest classification accuracy, achieving an Overall Accuracy (OA) of 91.84% and a Kappa Coefficient (KC) of 0.86 in 2023, thereby affirming its efficacy for multi-temporal land use and land cover mapping. The Decision Tree exhibited competitive performance in 2010 (87.36% OA, a KC of 0.79) but showed diminished stability in later years. The SVM displayed middling performance, particularly excelling in the classification of urban areas (about 94%) but exhibiting reduced accuracy for forest regions. This analysis emphasises the efficacy of GEE and Python libraries in analysing large satellite imagery and the proficiency of DT and RF models in land use and land cover classification. The results can guide regional planning and land management policies, fostering sustainable development.

title: From Engineering Education to Professional Fit: A Second-Order Structural Model in a Municipal Context
abstract: Abstract Using covariance-based structural equation modeling (CB-SEM), this study examined the relationship between undergraduate civil engineering education and professional fit among civil engineers employed in municipalities. Unlike previous studies that primarily conceptualized professional fit in terms of technical competence, this study modeled professional fit as a second-order latent construct reflected by two complementary first-order dimensions: technical fit (TECH_FIT) and institutional fit (INST_FIT). Data were collected through a nationwide questionnaire survey of 758 civil engineers working in metropolitan, provincial, and district municipalities across Turkey. The measurement model demonstrated satisfactory reliability, convergent validity, and discriminant validity. The structural model showed that perceived adequacy of undergraduate civil engineering education was positively and significantly associated with professional fit ( β = 0.826 , p < 0.001 ), explaining 68.3% of its variance ( R 2 = 0.683 ). The second-order measurement model further indicated that professional fit was strongly represented by both technical fit (standardized loading = 0.927) and institutional fit (standardized loading = 0.925), supporting the proposed multidimensional conceptualization. These findings suggest that professional preparedness in municipal engineering practice involves both technical competencies and institutional capabilities required for public sector engineering environments. The findings of the study contribute to the engineering education literature by providing empirical support for a second-order conceptualization of professional fit and by extending current understanding of the relationship between undergraduate engineering education and perceived professional preparedness in municipal practice. The proposed framework may also provide a useful basis for future studies examining professional fit across different engineering disciplines and organizational contexts.
