title: Efficacy Comparison of Inorganic-Matrix-Based Systems for Concrete Column Confinement: A Large Experimental Investigation
abstract: Abstract This study investigates the confinement of concrete cylinders using both fabric-reinforced cementitious matrix/mortar (FRCM) systems and engineered cementitious composites (ECCs), providing a broader perspective than previous research, which typically focuses on a single confinement strategy. The aim is to evaluate the respective contributions of the matrix and the fabric to overall confinement effectiveness, comparing various configurations of FRCM and ECC systems to assess their impact on axial strength and ductility relative to unconfined reference specimens. Through an extensive experimental campaign involving axial compression tests and strain compatibility measurements {varied variables are the type of fiber [carbon, glass, poly(p-phenylene-2,6-benzobisoxazole) (PBO), and steel], number of plies (one or two), and matrix properties (different compressive strength grades)}, the research reveals that the matrix plays a decisive role in strain transfer and confinement efficiency. The results demonstrated that multiply configurations significantly enhance confinement performance, particularly in brittle matrices. Moreover, ductile matrices such as those reinforced with short steel fibers can provide effective confinement even without fabric reinforcement. The congruency check confirmed that strain compatibility is a critical factor influencing confinement efficiency, beyond strength or ductility alone.

title: Lightweight Spatio-Temporal Attention Graph Neural Networks for Construction Investment Valuation: Higher Fidelity than GAT on Large-Scale Data
abstract: Abstract Investment decision-making in construction is influenced by a broad spectrum of uncertainties, encompassing fiscal unpredictability and geopolitical instability. Canonical valuation techniques, grounded in rational expectations, often prove insufficient in accounting for abnormal market behaviors. In response, we propose a lightweight spatio-temporal valuation architecture that incorporates graph neural network (GNN) attention modules and temporal gating operations to evaluate and classify construction projects by ex-ante investment attractiveness as defined by a decision-theoretic proxy: a structured expert-elicited multicriteria score intended to approximate early-stage portfolio screening under uncertainty (i.e., limited information at inception and time-varying macrorisk). This research utilizes a curated corpus of 12,991 global construction initiatives (downsampled from 33,684 records), supplemented with expert-formulated multicriteria rankings and Euler Hermes–derived sovereign risk ratings. Each construction project is encoded as a node within a graph, where connections are established based on regional locality and funding modality, facilitating the modeling of implicit spatial-financial dependencies. The proposed architecture family integrates a lightweight spatio-temporal attention-based graph neural network (STAGNN), which utilizes simple cosine-similarity attention mechanism for dynamic neighborhood weighting, with gated recurrent units (GRUs) to learn the temporal progression of project-level features. We formulate and evaluate multiple hybrid configurations, including different GRU variants, and nongated STAGNN variations and other standard baselines like graph convolutional network (GCN)–recurrent neural network (RNN) and graph attention network (GAT)–long short-term memory (LSTM) models in binary classification tasks (distinguishing very high from premium investment potential). Results show strong performance gains from incorporating STAGNN into spatio-temporal architectures. STAGNN reached 96% accuracy and F1 scores, recording 99% area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), underscoring the potential of a high-fidelity yet low-complexity model in minimizing false classifications and preserving high model fidelity. STAGNN’s cosine-attention eliminates dense layers and avoids multilayer perceptrons (MLPs) and multiheads, reducing parameter count and architectural complexity. It outperforms the GRU-enhanced AGNN-GAT model in prior study while keeping the design lightweight. Crucially, the attention mechanism alleviated over smoothing, preserving node-level distinctiveness in complex network topologies. The proposed framework enables rapid, data-driven investment flagging, obviating reliance on manual input, thereby advancing portfolio design strategies and risk analytics.

title: Hybrid care model in kidney transplantation: a safe strategy in times of pandemic
abstract: ABSTRACT Introduction: The COVID-19 pandemic required rapid changes in hospital workflows. Telemedicine care models have become fundamental tools in this scenario, reducing the movement of individuals and the risk of COVID-19 transmission. However, there is a lack of equivalence studies on telemedicine regarding relevant clinical outcomes in kidney transplant patients. This study aims to evaluate the equivalence of the hybrid model of outpatient care for kidney transplant patients compared with the standard in-person model in terms of the number of hospitalizations, loss of graft function, and deaths over a one-year follow-up. Methods: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of kidney transplant recipients, over the age of 18, with a functioning graft, receiving immunosuppressive therapy for one to ten years at a tertiary hospital in southern Brazil, allocated to the in-person group (April 2016) or the hybrid group (April 2020), employing two one-sided tests (TOST) and equivalence testing to compare hospitalization rates, graft survival, and mortality. The follow-up duration was one year. Data were extracted from electronic and physical medical records. Results: The study comprised 194 patients (56.7% male, median age 54 years). Variables analyzed included demographic, laboratory, and clinical data. Transplant times were different between groups: 3.6 ± 2.50 years (in-person) vs. 4.3 ± 2.35 years (hybrid model) (p = 0.049). Equivalence was found in hospitalization rates (p = 0.038), graft survival (p = 0.0359), and mortality (p = 0.007) between care models. Conclusion: Hybrid care for kidney transplant patients has shown equivalence to in-person visits concerning critical clinical outcomes during the pandemic. This suggests its viability as a permanent care model. Further studies are warranted to reinforce these findings and examine long-term implications.

title: Multiscenario Simulation and Prediction of Urban Green Space in the Changle District of Fuzhou City, China, Based on Multiobjective Optimization and a GeoSOS-FLUS Model
abstract: Abstract Green spaces in densely urbanized areas along China’s southeast coast generally face spatial competition between ecological protection and development intensity, as well as conflicts between policy-oriented and market-driven values. Among them, Changle District in Fuzhou City, as the core area of the coastal new city, needs to coordinate its green space system to address complex three-dimensional problems. To explore the optimal configuration of green spaces under different ecological constraints and achieve a balance between ecological, economic, and social benefits, this paper takes Changle District in Fuzhou City as the research area, with 2020 as the base year, and innovatively combines a multiobjective optimization model with the Geographic Simulation and Optimization System–Future Land Use Simulation (GeoSOS-FLUS) model. The former is used to balance multiple objectives such as ecological conservation, economic development, and social needs, generating optimal allocation schemes. The latter precisely simulates the dynamic evolution of green spaces based on these schemes. Together, they overcome the limitations of traditional models, which cannot account for economic and ecological benefits when simulating complex urban land use. Based on this model combination, this paper simulates and predicts the area structure, spatial configuration, and target benefits of green space in Changle District in 2030 under ecological high-, medium-, and low-constraint scenarios. The results reveal the following: (1) In terms of area structure, the area of cropland and unused land in the three scenarios is smaller than the current value in 2020, while forest land and grassland have increased, water has been effectively protected, and construction land has gradually increased as ecological constraints have been relaxed. (2) In terms of spatial distribution, the area of cropland in the north, west, and central parts of the study area decreased significantly in all three scenarios. At the same time, the increase in forest land and grassland was concentrated in the north and west, and the rise in water was focused on the central part of the study area. The area of construction land in the south and west decreased slightly under the ecological high- and medium-constraint scenarios. At the same time, it increased around the center of the study area under the low ecological constraint scenario. (3) From the perspective of target benefits, under the high-ecological-constraint scenario, the ecological benefits and economic benefits are 4.122 and 94.545 billion yuan, respectively, which is a significant increase compared with the ecological benefits in 2020, while the economic benefits have slightly decreased. Under the medium-ecological-constraint scenario, the ecological and economic benefits are 4.067 and 104.023 billion yuan, respectively, representing significant increases compared with 2020. Under the low-ecological-constraint scenario, the ecological benefits and economic benefits are 4.009 and 112.945 billion yuan, respectively, which represents a slight increase in ecological benefits compared to 2020 but a significant increase in economic benefits. The conclusions of this study can be applied to urban green space planning practices, providing comprehensive support for decision-makers in formulating scientific and reasonable green space allocation strategies under different ecological constraints and helping to achieve sustainable urban development goals.

title: Lifelong Learning in AI: A Fuzzy Logic-Based Approach to Knowledge Retention
abstract: Lifelong learning in AI aims to enable systems to continuously acquire and adapt knowledge over timewithout forgetting previously learned information. This study explores the effectiveness of integratingfuzzy logic into lifelong learning frameworks and compares it with traditional methods such as neuralnetworks and reinforcement learning. Through experimental evaluation, we assessed key performancemetrics including task accuracy, knowledge retention, and adaptability. Results demonstrate that fuzzylogic-based AI significantly outperforms traditional methods, achieving higher accuracy across multipletasks and exhibiting superior knowledge retention with reduced catastrophic forgetting. Specifically,fuzzy logic-based AI maintains accuracies of 93%, 85%, and 80% for successive tasks, compared todeclining performance in neural networks and reinforcement learning. Additionally, fuzzy logic shows amarked reduction in knowledge loss (15%) and enhanced adaptability (80%). These findings underscorethe potential of fuzzy logic to enhance lifelong learning systems by providing a more flexible and resilientapproach to knowledge management and incremental learning.

title: Evaluating Continual Learning Techniques in Edge AI for Real-Time Applications
abstract: This research investigates the efficacy of various continual learning techniques—Elastic WeightConsolidation (EWC), Experience Replay, and Knowledge Distillation—within the framework of EdgeAI for real-time applications. Continual learning, crucial for adapting AI models to new data whilepreserving previously acquired knowledge, presents unique challenges when deployed on resource-constrained edge devices. This study evaluates these techniques based on key performance metricsincluding task accuracy, old task accuracy, latency, resource usage, and adaptability. The findings revealthat Experience Replay excels in maintaining high task accuracy and adaptability, albeit with increasedresource demands. EWC provides a balanced approach with moderate performance and resource usagebut shows slightly lower adaptability. Knowledge Distillation offers an efficient solution with goodperformance and minimal computational overhead, making it suitable for edge environments with strictresource constraints. These insights guide the selection of continual learning methods tailored to thespecific needs of real-time Edge AI applications

title: AI-Based Performance Analysis of Renewable Energy Systems for Sustainable Power Generation
abstract: The growing demand for clean and reliable energy has accelerated the adoption of renewable energysystems such as solar photovoltaic and wind power technologies. However, the inherent variabilityof renewable resources poses significant challenges in performance prediction, system optimization,and reliable power generation. This study presents an artificial intelligence–based framework forperformance analysis of renewable energy systems aimed at supporting sustainable power generation.Operational and environmental data are utilized to develop machine learning models capable ofcapturing complex, nonlinear relationships between system inputs and energy output. The AI-basedapproach is evaluated against conventional analytical methods using performance indicators suchas power output, efficiency, prediction accuracy, and response time. The results demonstrate that AI-driven models significantly improve prediction accuracy, reduce analysis time, and enhance systemperformance assessment under varying operating conditions. The findings highlight the potential ofartificial intelligence to improve operational efficiency, support intelligent energy management, andstrengthen the integration of renewable energy systems into sustainable power networks.

title: Predictive Modeling of Material Properties Using Nanotechnology and Artificial Intelligence Techniques
abstract: Accurate prediction of material properties is essential for accelerating the development of advancedengineering materials, particularly those incorporating nanoscale features. Traditional experimentaland physics-based modeling approaches, while reliable, are often limited by high computational costand the complexity of capturing nonlinear nanoscale interactions. This study presents an integratedpredictive modeling framework that combines nanotechnology-derived material descriptors withartificial intelligence techniques to estimate key material properties. Nanoscale parameters such asparticle size, volume fraction, and structural characteristics are used as inputs to train machine learningmodels capable of learning complex structure–property relationships. The performance of AI-basedmodels is evaluated and compared with conventional empirical and physics-based approaches. Resultsdemonstrate that the artificial intelligence–driven framework achieves higher prediction accuracy andsignificantly reduced computational effort while maintaining consistency with experimental observations.The proposed approach highlights the potential of combining nanotechnology and artificial intelligenceto support efficient material design and optimization in advanced engineering applications.

title: Automated Detection of Counterfeit Indian Currency by Xception CNN and Edge Image Capture with ESP32
abstract: This paper explores the application of machine learning (ML) in detecting counterfeit Indian currencyusing the Xception deep learning model, which analyzes images to distinguish genuine notes fromfake ones. Out of the entire dataset, 70% fuelled the training phase, 20% guided validation, and thefinal 10% was reserved for testing to evaluate the model's performance comprehensively. Performanceassessment relied on indicators like correctness and specificity to measure how well the model did.The Xception model achieved an impressive 99% accuracy during training but showed limitations invalidation, performing at only 10%. These challenges highlight issues like dataset imbalance and theneed for effective feature extraction to enhance reliability. The findings underline the potential of MLin aiding banks and law enforcement agencies in identifying counterfeit currency efficiently. However,the study also identifies key areas for improvement, including addressing data imbalances and refiningthe model to improve validation effectiveness. Next-stage exploration will focus on enhancing themodel's robustness, incorporating additional features, and transitioning the model toward real-worldapplications.This research demonstrates the promise of ML in tackling the growing problem of counterfeit currencyand sets a foundation for further advancements in this domain.

title: Fuzzy-Based Decision Support Systems for Disaster Management in Smart Cities
abstract: In the context of smart cities, effective disaster management is paramount for ensuring public safetyand resilience against natural calamities. This research presents a novel fuzzy-based decision supportsystem (DSS) designed to enhance disaster response capabilities compared to traditional DSS models. Byintegrating real-time data from IoT sensors, social media, and meteorological forecasts, the fuzzy-basedapproach adeptly handles uncertainties and ambiguities inherent in disaster scenarios. Experimentalresults indicate that the fuzzy-based DSS significantly improves response times, achieving reductionsof up to 55% compared to traditional systems, while also enhancing decision-making accuracy torates as high as 92%. Moreover, the fuzzy system demonstrates superior resource allocation efficiencyand garners higher user satisfaction ratings. These findings underscore the efficacy of fuzzy logic intransforming disaster management practices, positioning it as a critical component for the developmentof resilient smart city infrastructures.

title: Impact of Digital Transformation and AI-Enabled Management Practices on Organizational Performance
abstract: This study examines how digital transformation and AI-enabled management practices jointlyinfluence organizational performance. Drawing on digital transformation literature and research onAI capability and algorithmic management, the study proposes that performance gains from digitaltransformation are strongest when AI is embedded into managerial routines such as decision-support,workforce planning, monitoring, and performance evaluation. The research framework conceptualizesdigital transformation maturity as the foundation that enables data integration and process digitization,while AI-enabled management practices act as a mechanism translating these digital capabilities intomeasurable outcomes. Comparative results indicate that organizations with higher levels of digitaltransformation and stronger AI-enabled management practices demonstrate superior performanceacross key indicators including productivity, operating cost reduction, decision-making speed, revenuegrowth, and innovation output, highlighting the role of AI-driven managerial redesign in strengtheningtransformation benefits.

title: Effectiveness of AI-Based Learning Tools in Improving Engineering Mathematics Understanding
abstract: Engineering mathematics is fundamental to engineering education, yet many students struggle toachieve conceptual clarity and problem-solving proficiency through traditional teaching methodsalone. This study investigates the effectiveness of AI-based learning tools in improving engineeringmathematics understanding among undergraduate engineering students. An AI-assisted learningenvironment incorporating adaptive practice, intelligent feedback, and personalized learning pathwayswas implemented alongside conventional classroom instruction. Student performance was evaluatedusing pre-test and post-test assessments, learning outcome metrics, and engagement indicators. Theresults show that students using AI-based tools achieved significantly higher post-test scores, improvedconceptual understanding, greater problem-solving accuracy, and reduced error rates compared tothose relying solely on traditional instruction. Increased engagement and sustained learning activityfurther highlight the benefits of AI-supported learning. The findings demonstrate that AI-based learningtools, when integrated with conventional teaching, offer an effective approach to enhancing engineeringmathematics education.

title: Analyzing the Role of Edge Computing in Enhancing AI Applications in Healthcare
abstract: This research investigates the role of edge computing in enhancing artificial intelligence (AI) applicationswithin the healthcare sector. By comparing edge computing to traditional cloud computing, the studyfocuses on key performance metrics such as latency, bandwidth consumption, data privacy, real-timeprocessing efficiency, storage costs, and response time for critical alerts. The results demonstrate thatedge computing significantly reduces latency and bandwidth usage while improving data security andreal-time processing capabilities, making it a superior choice for AI-powered healthcare applicationssuch as diagnostics, predictive analytics, personalized medicine, and remote patient monitoring. Thefindings highlight the potential of edge computing to address the growing demands of AI in healthcareby providing more efficient, secure, and responsive solutions, ultimately improving patient outcomes andoperational efficiency in healthcare environments.

title: "AI-INTEGRATED LEARNING MANAGEMENT SYSTEMS (LMS) : IMPACT ON PRIMARY SCHOOL STUDENT'S ACADEMIC PERFORMANCE"
abstract: This study investigates the effectiveness of Artificial Intelligence (AI)-enhanced Learning Management Systems (LMS) in improving academic achievement, engagement, and critical thinking among primary school students. Despite growing adoption of AI tools in educational settings, findings reveal limited measurable benefits at the primary level. A mixed-method, cross-sectional design was employed with data collected from 120 students using academic assessments, LMS usage logs, classroom observations, and teacher interviews. Regression analysis showed weak relationships between AI tools—personalized learning, adaptive assessments, and intelligent feedback—and academic performance (R = 0.091, R² = 0.008), with no significant predictors (p > 0.05). Similarly, system log analyses found no significant correlations between LMS usage indicators (logins, time spent) and engagement, suggesting quantitative metrics alone cannot capture the multifaceted nature of engagement. A weak, non-significant positive correlation between personalized learning and critical thinking (r = 0.159, p = 0.082) was also observed. These findings align with existing critiques emphasizing the importance of pedagogical readiness, teacher training, and contextualized implementation in AI-driven education. The study highlights the need for multidimensional engagement measures and longitudinal mixed-method research to understand AI's long-term impact. While AI technologies hold promise, their effective integration in primary classrooms requires cautious optimism, professional development, and institutional support.

title: Case Report: Behavioural Changes in a Feline with Cytauxzoonosis
abstract: This case report describes a one-year-old male cat diagnosed with Cytauxzoon spp., who exhibited behavioural symptoms typically associated with illness, including lethargy and decreased appetite, prior to treatment. As treatment was instated, the cat developed a noticeable licking psychosis amongst other behavioral stress signs. The stress signs escalated daily despite the administration of appropriate medical interventions, while his clinical condition showed little improvement. In response to the escalating behavioral issues, we transitioned the treatment environment from the clinic to the home setting. This was meant to assess the impact of familiar surroundings on both clinical and behavioral outcomes. Remarkably, upon shifting the treatment setting, the cat began to exhibit positive behavioral changes along with a gradual improvement in clinical signs. These changes occurred after 2 weeks of at-home management. This case illustrates the importance of addressing both clinical treatment and behavioral manifestations when managing patients. Our findings highlight the necessity for veterinary practitioners to consider the psychological well-being alongside physical health in order to enhance the overall success of treatment protocols.

title: Measuring Student Comprehension of Animal Behaviour Concepts
abstract: This study evaluated the effectiveness of students' skills in behavioural assessment of animals as a teaching tool, specifically identifying errors in their evaluations and measuring their improvement over time. A group of 45 students assessed the behaviour of five distinct animals weekly over a five-week period, utilizing a standardized 5-point behavioural checklist to score each animal. The study compared students' ratings against those of their instructors, as well as among peer evaluations, to determine the consistency and reliability of their assessments. Analysis of the collected data assessed the degree of alignment between students and instructor evaluations, highlighted discrepancies, and identified patterns of improvement in students’ scoring accuracy throughout the assessment period. This evaluation method aimed to enhance understanding of the learning curve in behavioural assessment and improve pedagogical approaches that equipped students with the necessary skills in animal welfare evaluation. The findings can contribute towards refining educational methodologies in animal behaviour studies and promoting ongoing improvement in student assessment capabilities.

title: Administrative audit of a hotel company in the State of Veracruz
abstract: One of the strategic tools to evaluate the efficiency, effectiveness and congruence of the administrative process of companies is the administrative audit. The results obtained from the administrative audit applied to a hotel located in the state of Veracruz were analyzed, in order to identify areas of opportunity and propose improvement actions aimed at organizational strengthening. The research was developed under a descriptive and diagnostic approach, using observation techniques, interviews, documentary analysis and evaluation cards structured according to the stages of the administrative process. The results show relevant strengths in the organization, management and control phases, particularly in the definition of functions, work environment, use of technology and information systems. Significant weaknesses are detected in the planning stage, derived from the formal absence of mission, vision, objectives, strategies and SWOT analysis, which limits the strategic orientation of the company.

title: Evaluation of mechanical properties of starch-gelatin-sargassum polymers based on neural networks
abstract: In biodegradable polymer research, starch, gelatin, and Sargassum algae waste are gaining attention as a potential solution to mitigate the environmental impact of conventional plastics. This study, conducted at Universidad Tecnológica de Tula-Tepeji, evaluated the mechanical properties of a polymer composed of these components using a CT3 texture analyzer, with neural network models employed to predict such properties. Polymers were prepared with varying Sargassum concentrations, and their mechanical response under tensile loading was analyzed to estimate Young's modulus. The casting process effectively integrated Sargassum into the polymer, offering a potential eco-friendly alternative. Neural network predictions of the material's behavior proved accurate, demonstrating the usefulness of this approach in materials research. These findings support incorporating additional data and Sargassum variations in future work to further enhance predictive capability.

title: Conceptual Design of an Ergonomic Postgraduate Classroom: “Strategies and Effects on Students’ Physical Well-Being and Academic Performance”
abstract: This research addresses ergonomic deficiencies in postgraduate classrooms that negatively affect students’ physical well-being and academic performance. The study aims to develop a conceptual ergonomic classroom design adapted to the Mexican higher education context. A participatory systemic approach based on Soft Systems Methodology (SSM) was applied, integrating ergonomic regulatory criteria from ISO 9241-5 (International Organization for Standardization, 1998; Secretaría del Trabajo y Previsión Social, 2008) and NOM-025-STPS-2008 Secretaría del Trabajo y Previsión Social (2008). The methodology included problem diagnosis through observation, interviews, surveys, and documentary analysis; construction of conceptual models considering anthropometric, lighting, acoustic, accessibility, and technological variables; comparison between the current classroom and the proposed model; and refinement based on cultural and technical feasibility. The results show a significant improvement in ergonomic compliance levels, increasing from low to high performance across all evaluated criteria. The proposed model provides a replicable framework for designing ergonomic learning environments that promote physical well-being and support academic performance in postgraduate education.

title: Artificial Intelligence: Competencies for design in emerging creative environments
abstract: The study, titled From Artificial Intelligence: Competencies for Design in Emerging Creative Environments, aims to determine the competencies linked to the use of Artificial Intelligence in the training of designers, as well as to examine its impact on the professional environment. The advancement of AI has reconfigured not only the tools for design practice, but also the essential dynamics of the creative process. In emerging human-AI collaboration [HAIC] scenarios, these systems operate as cooperative agents and not merely as support tools. However, even though design students are progressively incorporating these technologies into their practice, a gap persists in the development of fundamental competencies for establishing effective interaction with these systems. Therefore, the need to strengthen disciplinary training through competencies that integrate critical interpretation, collaborative interaction, ethical and metacognitive reflection, in addition to specialized technical mastery is recognized. Based on the above, this research is structured around a comprehensive review of scientific literature, analysing studies retrieved from specialized databases in both design and higher education. The methodology will adopt the PRISMA [2021] systematic review protocol, which will ensure a rigorous process for the identification, selection, and synthesis of emerging competencies. The findings will be presented through graphic visualizations, and the discussion will incorporate relevant case studies. Ultimately, the study aims to offer an in-depth theoretical and methodological framework for future lines of research, highlighting the strategic role of AI competencies in the academic achievement and professional development of designers. These competencies are essential for overcoming limitations related to the originality, quality, and coherence of creative proposals, indispensable elements for competitive performance in educational and professional contexts.

title: Artificial Intelligence applied to direct current motors as a continuous improvement in their monitoring and performance
abstract: Currently, manufacturing and artificial intelligence are fundamental for organizations, providing optimal decision-making, accurate maintenance forecasts, and reduced manufacturing equipment costs, resulting in higher-quality production. The implementation of new technologies, such as neural networks applied to motors in transient states, expands the possibilities for achieving continuous improvement in company productivity. This research proposes the use of neural networks to control the speed and position of a DC motor as part of a continuous improvement in efficiency levels and real-time monitoring, allowing for data analysis and simulation of automatic control systems. The methodology used is non-experimental and cross-sectional, simulating a control design interacting with an neural network in the MATLAB programming environment and with a LabVIEW module interacting with a Raspberry Pi computer, ideal for data acquisition and control.

title: ANOVA Methodology for a comparative study of the adoption level of information technologies and computer systems in MSEs
abstract: This chapter presents the results of a study measuring the level of adoption of information technologies and computer systems in the operations and resource management of 25 micro and small enterprises (MSEs) located in the municipalities of Atlautla, Ozumba, and Tepetlixpa in eastern Mexico State. The study employed a quantitative, cross-sectional, descriptive-comparative design, using mean differences. Data collection utilized items from the sixth dimension of the instrument developed by the Latin American Network of Administration and Business [RELAyN], [Aguilar, et al., 2018] which included dichotomous and Likert-scale questions. The results support proposals aimed at strengthening the digital capacity of MSEs in rural and semi-urban areas, emphasizing public policies that improve digital infrastructure and facilitate access to technological training, as well as fostering partnerships between higher education institutions in the region and the productive units.

title: A Scoping Review Protocol on Artificial Intelligence Adoption and Employee Well-being: A Job Demands–Resources Perspective from Academia and Practice
abstract: Objective This scoping review aims to systematically examine academic research and specific grey literature from professional resource sites to provide an understanding of how Artificial Intelligence (AI) impacts employee well-being within organisational settings through the lens of Job Demands-Resources (JD-R) theory. Research Question What evidence exists on how the adoption of artificial intelligence affects employee well-being, viewed through the job demands-resources theory, from both academic and practitioner perspectives? Introduction The fast-track adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based technologies has significantly reshaped workplaces. There has been a growing imperative to understand how employees’ adoption of such emerging AI technologies affects employee well-being. To date, the mapping of this relationship based on the dual pathways of Job-demands and resources (JD-R) from the academic and practitioner perspectives have not been explored. A scoping review comparing insights from both perspectives on the use of AI technologies and the impact on employee well-being based on the JD-R theory will reveal research gaps that can benefit both communities. Methods and Analysis The scoping review will follow the methodological guidelines of Arksey & O’Malley (2005) framework, and the updated guidance Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) (2024) will be used to conducting the scoping review. Academic articles will be sourced through electronic databases, including PsycINFO, Scopus, and Web of Science. Additionally, grey literature will be retrieved from professional resource sites such as the International Labour Organisation (ILO) and consulting firms, including Accenture and Deloitte. Search limits will include a date range of 2001 to the present day and will only include articles that are in English. Pilot testing of 25 articles will be employed for title and abstract screening, full-text screening and data charting/extraction. Two reviewers will participate in each stage of screening and extraction and will be conducted independently with a third reviewer responsible for resolving conflict. Ethics and Dissemination This scoping review generates new knowledge from published and publicly available literature. Therefore, ethics review and approval will not be necessary. Dissemination of the review findings will include publication in peer-reviewed journal, with all team members committed to facilitate knowledge sharing through professional networking platforms and public-facing media. Key insights will also be shared with professional associations and industry stakeholders. In addition, findings will inform curriculum development and be integrated into professional learning contexts, offering learners with contemporary knowledge and real-world applications.

title: Catalytic enhancement of biogas production from organic waste using Cobalt Ferrite Nanoparticles
abstract: The improvement of biogas production from organic waste is a key objective in sustainable waste management and renewable energy generation. In this study, cobalt ferrite nanoparticles [CoFe₂O₄-NPs] were synthesized via a hydrothermal method and evaluated as catalytic additives in a laboratory-scale anaerobic bioreactor. The effect of nanoparticle incorporation was assessed using 50 g of organic fruit waste in a 2.46 L prototype reactor. Biogas production was monitored over 48 h under natural solar irradiation. The control system generated 12 cm³ of biogas, whereas the addition of 0.5 mL and 1 mL of a 0.1 M nanoparticle dispersion increased production to 126.25 cm³ and 157.81 cm³, respectively. These values correspond to a 10.5–13.2-fold enhancement relative to the non-catalyzed condition. The results demonstrate a clear dose dependent catalytic effect and suggest that cobalt ferrite nanoparticles promote accelerated degradation of organic matter during anaerobic fermentation.

title: The Role of ChatGPT in Research from a Student Perspective
abstract: Artificial Intelligence [AI] is gaining importance in the field of education, especially in the generation of information through automated systems. The objective of this study is to characterize the ChatGPT variable in research. A quantitative methodology with a descriptive scope and cross-sectional cohort was used to collect data from a sample of 24 students using a questionnaire. The findings characterize the tool as useful for generating research topics [70.8%] and new topics accurately [54.2%], in research papers [70.8%], and in constructing literature reviews [50.3%], effectively [70%], optimizing search time for literature review construction [70.8%]. The study's contribution lies in identifying the fundamental attributes that should be included in training programs to maximize the potential of ChatGPT in the academic context.

title: Strategic energy efficiency plan aligned with artificial intelligence. Case study: CETis 91
abstract: This paper describes the design and implementation of an AI-powered energy efficiency strategic plan aligned with the Project Management Institute [PMI] guidelines. The plan aimed to optimize electricity consumption, reduce operating costs, and decrease the carbon footprint of a high school. A mixed-methods approach was employed in this research, using a case study at CETis 91. This study was supported by PMI processes, energy management systems [EMS], and data analysis using sensors and artificial intelligence tools to identify consumption patterns. The results demonstrate how a strategic plan allows for the precise identification of opportunities to improve environmental management, from replacing lighting with LED technology in high traffic areas to promoting the adoption of energy-efficient practices by the school community. Finally, the paper describes how the integration of strategic planning, project management, artificial intelligence, and energy management systems fosters systematic, replicable, and sustainable institutional energy management in public educational settings.

title: Nature of the sense of belonging in Higher Education
abstract: The objective of this article was to analyze the relationship between the sense of belonging and perceived academic performance in a population of 8th-semester students of the Accounting Degree at the Academic Unit of Accounting and Administration [UACyA] of the Autonomous University of Nayarit [UAN]. The study was conducted using a quantitative approach with a non-experimental, cross sectional design, focusing the analysis on descriptive statistics. The results reveal an operational dissociation within the belonging construct: while the affective factor, measured by institutional pride, is perceived as the primary driver of motivation for high academic performance, as well as the social dimension [interaction with peers and faculty]. It is concluded that the sense of belonging among these students is grounded in an affective and symbolic commitment to the institution and professional achievement, rather than in active social integration.

title: A methodological framework for AI-Assisted design and fabrication of patient-specific cranial plug prostheses
abstract: This paper presents an artificial intelligence-assisted methodological framework for the design and fabrication of patient-specific cranial plug prostheses from computed tomography data. The proposed workflow integrates AI-assisted semantic segmentation, three dimensional reconstruction, topological repair of the anatomical model, geometric parameter extraction for prosthesis generation, and an expert-in-the-loop validation stage to ensure clinical viability prior to fabrication. The methodology was validated through a comparative analysis against a traditional manual fabrication procedure, using a small-scale cranial perforation as a test case with high geometric fit requirements. Results showed a substantial reduction in fabrication time and an improvement in the anatomical fit of the AI-generated device. Overall, the findings support the proposed framework as a replicable, precise, and efficient alternative for patient-specific prosthesis fabrication in clinically demanding settings.

title: Automatic cephalometric landmarking on CBCT volumes using depth-map non rigid registration
abstract: This study developed and evaluated an automatic method for 3D cephalometric landmark localization in CBCT data using surface-based depth map representations and non-rigid registration. Craniofacial geometry was represented through structured depth maps, and a template skull was registered to target data using the Optimal Step Non-Rigid Iterative Closest Point algorithm. For 15 surface landmarks, the mean 3D localization error was 2.07 mm, which increased to 2.87 mm for all 18 landmarks due to higher errors in internal structures like the Sella and Basion. Accuracy was highest for anterior midline landmarks and lower for bilateral landmarks in complex regions. With a processing time of 1 to 4 minutes per case, this surface-based approach provides clinically acceptable accuracy for surface landmarks and effectively reduces manual annotation time when combined with expert refinement.

title: Comparison of the effects of AI-generated music on emotional responses, aesthetic enjoyment, and perceived quality between musicians and non-musicians
abstract: This study investigates how emotional responses, aesthetic enjoyment, and perceived quality elicited by artificial intelligence (AI)-generated music differ between musicians and non-musicians using a mixed-methods research design. To conceptualize the effects of technological mediation on musical experience, the study adopts a multilayered theoretical framework encompassing Meyer's theory of musical emotion, Huron's expectation model, the Geneva Emotional Music Scale (GEMS), Bourdieu's theory of cultural capital, and Benjamin's concept of mechanical reproducibility. The study included a total of 64 participants, consisting of 32 musicians and 32 non-musicians. Data were collected using the Positive and Negative Affect Schedule (PANAS), the Geneva Emotional Music Scale (GEMS), and the Toronto Empathy Questionnaire (TEQ), while the qualitative dimension was enriched through semi-structured interviews and focus group discussions. Descriptive statistics indicated that AI-generated music produced moderate levels of emotional arousal and aesthetic enjoyment. MANOVA and post hoc multiple comparison analyses revealed that non-musicians reported significantly higher levels of pleasure (M = 4.12) than musicians (M = 3.24), whereas the opposite pattern was observed for inspiration. Among musicians, a positive correlation was found between pleasure and inspiration (r = .284), while a negative correlation emerged among non-musicians (r = −.357). Qualitative findings indicated that although AI-generated music was perceived as technically impressive, emotional engagement remained limited due to a perceived lack of authenticity. While musicians appreciated its technical compositional competence, they adopted a more critical stance regarding emotional depth. In contrast, non-musicians reported greater aesthetic pleasure but experienced lower levels of creative inspiration. These findings are consistent with theoretical perspectives concerning cultural capital and the social construction of aesthetic judgment.

title: Development of methodological skills for violin and viola teaching at UAZ
abstract: Teaching methodology is a discipline that forms part of the curriculum in the Bachelor of Music program; in the specific case of the violin and viola, within the Academic Unit of Arts of the Autonomous University of Zacatecas [UAA-UAZ] , it gains relevance through the impact it has on students’ future professional practice. His context provides the motivation for the present article, which aims to reflect on the development of methodological skills for violin and viola teaching within the course of Instrument Teaching Methodology, Violin/Viola at UAA UAZ, grounded in both teacher and student perspectives. A qualitative methodology was adopted, employing documentary analysis, experiential analysis, unstructured interviews, and pedagogical observation. Collectively, these methods made it possible to underscore both the importance of discipline within the curriculum and the impact it has on the formation of methodological skills in future professionals.

title: The Importance of electromobility for the Country's development
abstract: Electromobility represents one of the most significant transformations in contemporary transportation systems and constitutes a fundamental strategy for countries’ sustainable development. The objective of this research is to analyze the importance of electromobility as a strategic element for the country’s economic, social, environmental, and technological development. The methodology employed was qualitative in nature, specifically documentary-descriptive, involving a systematic review of scientific literature, institutional reports, and specialized international reports on electric mobility and the energy transition. The findings show that electromobility has a positive impact on reducing greenhouse gas emissions, improves energy efficiency, drives industrial value chains, and generates opportunities for technological innovation.

title: Water quality prediction systems using IoT and Machine Learning: A systematic review
abstract: This systematic review analyzes 52 studies (2018–2026) on integrated IoT and Machine Learning systems for water quality prediction in aquaculture. Results show that Random Forest achieves accuracy above 94 % in survival classification, while hybrid Deep Learning models such as CNN-SA-BiSRU reach R² = 0.9765 for dissolved oxygen prediction. The most monitored parameters are pH (98.2 %), temperature (92.9 %), and dissolved oxygen (62.5 %). Critical gaps are identified: scarcity of species-specific datasets for larvae and fry, predominance of single target models, and limited validation under real production conditions. The review concludes that IoT-ML integration has demonstrated technical feasibility, but further applied research is required for effective adoption in commercial aquaculture farms, particularly in resource constrained rural settings where most small-scale fish farming occurs.

title: Digital innovation for strategic decision-making in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs: integrating ERP systems, data analytics, and digital governance
abstract: This article analyzes the role of digital innovation in strategic decision-making within the Secretaría de Relaciones Exteriores, highlighting the integration of ERP systems, data analytics, and digital governance as key elements for institutional modernization. The objective was to identify how the incorporation of digital technologies contributes to strengthening operational efficiency, interoperability, and data-driven management in complex public organizations. The methodology adopted was qualitative, documentary, and analytical, based on the review of scientific literature, institutional reports, and specialized documents. The results show that the implementation of ERP systems, Business Intelligence tools, and digital engagement strategies promotes process automation, improves decision-making, and strengthens institutional transparency. The study proposes and theoretically supports an integrated digital innovation framework for digital innovation that supports institutional modernization, enhances strategic decision making, and promotes public value creation.

title: Hospitalization risk stratification in Mexican respiratory surveillance data: a retrospective analysis with interpretable machine learning
abstract: This retrospective study analyzes 219,023 records from Mexico’s open respiratory surveillance data to identify factors associated with hospitalization and evaluate hospitalization risk stratification using interpretable machine learning. After data quality review and preprocessing, 218,557 complete records were analyzed. Logistic regression was used to estimate interpretable odds ratios, threshold tuning was applied to improve recall, and Random Forest was used as a comparative predictive model. Pneumonia was the strongest factor associated with hospitalization, followed by COPD, diabetes, and hypertension. The baseline logistic regression model achieved 76.7% accuracy and 55.3% recall; threshold tuning increased recall to 71.1%, reducing false negatives. Random Forest achieved the best overall predictive balance, with 79.5% accuracy, 71.9% recall, and a 76.9% F1-score. These findings support the use of open surveillance data for interpretable public health analytics and future respiratory hospitalization monitoring.

title: AI, HR Governance, and Human Capital Risk in Indonesia’s Digital Banking: A Systematic Review
abstract: While AI is set to make banking faster and better, discussions often overlook its significant impact on human capital and governance. The current literature is still fragmented, largely addressing AI adoption, human resource management (HRM), and sustainability as independent domains, ignoring the structural risks that develop where they can overlap. This study explicitly addresses this gap by examining how AI simultaneously reorganises HR competencies, creates human capital risks, and necessitates governance practices consistent with sustainability goals. This research employs a systematic literature review (SLR) of 68 peer-reviewed articles obtained from three distinct streams of literature: banking, HRM, and sustainability, using the PRISMA 2020 protocol. Results challenge dominant techno-centric perspectives, suggesting that AI is not simply a tool for boosting productivity but rather an underlying structural driver of both human capital risk—algorithmic bias, lack of transparency and accountability—and worker vulnerability. What is more relevant about the study is that it provides a key takeaway: that without sound HR governance development, AI implementation may undermine organisational legitimacy and have ethical and sustainability impacts. Positioning HR governance as an integrative and corrective mechanism, this study provides a framework linking AI capability, human capital risk, and sustainability. This research provides a different perspective on the literature by shifting the debate around AI-enabled HR transformation from a technological issue to a governance problem that carries multifaceted ramifications toward sustainable digital banking, especially in developing economies such as Indonesia.

title: STUDI ETNOPEDAGOGI TENTANG PENDIDIKAN ANAK DALAM KELUARGA MASYARAKAT BATAK DI MEDAN DENAI BERBASIS NILAI-NILAI KEARIFAN LOKAL
abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) has significantly transformed educational practices, including the way students engage in academic writing. AI-assisted tools such as ChatGPT, Grammarly, QuillBot, Gemini, and other AI-powered applications are increasingly being used by students to support various stages of the writing process. These technologies provide assistance in generating ideas, correcting grammar, improving vocabulary, organizing content, and revising written texts. As digital technologies become more integrated into students’ daily lives, understanding how learners experience the use of AI-assisted tools in academic writing has become an important area of educational research. Therefore, this study aims to explore the experiences of SMA Dharmawangsa students in using AI-assisted tools for academic writing, identify the perceived benefits and challenges, and examine students’ perspectives on the role of AI in supporting their writing development.This study employed a qualitative approach using a phenomenological research design. The participants were students of SMA Dharmawangsa who had experience using AI-assisted tools in completing academic writing tasks. Participants were selected through purposive sampling based on specific criteria relevant to the research objectives. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews, observations, and documentation. The data were analyzed using the interactive model of Miles, Huberman, and Saldaña, which involved data reduction, data display, and conclusion drawing. To ensure the trustworthiness of the findings, triangulation, member checking, and peer debriefing were applied.The findings revealed that students generally had positive experiences using AI-assisted tools in academic writing. Students perceived AI technologies as useful learning resources that helped them generate ideas, improve grammar and vocabulary, organize essays, and revise their writing more effectively. The use of AI-assisted tools also increased students’ confidence and supported independent learning by providing immediate feedback during the writing process. Furthermore, students reported that AI technologies helped them complete writing tasks more efficiently and reduced difficulties commonly encountered in academic writing. However, several challenges were identified, including the tendency to rely excessively on AI-generated content, concerns regarding the accuracy of information provided by AI systems, and uncertainty about the ethical boundaries of AI use in academic work. Despite these challenges, most participants recognized the importance of using AI responsibly and maintaining originality in their writing.The study concludes that AI-assisted tools have significant potential to support students’ academic writing development when used appropriately. AI technologies can enhance writing quality, foster learner autonomy, and increase engagement in writing activities. Nevertheless, effective use of AI requires students to critically evaluate AI-generated suggestions and maintain academic integrity. The study proposes the concept of Responsible AI-Assisted Academic Writing, which emphasizes the role of AI as a learning companion rather than a replacement for students’ critical thinking and writing abilities. The findings contribute to the growing body of research on artificial intelligence in education and provide practical insights for teachers, schools, and policymakers in promoting ethical and effective AI integration in academic writing instruction.

title: Academic performance evaluation incorporating applied research within the ITIC Degree Program
abstract: Academic performance and student dropout are widely recognized as key indicators for assessing educational quality in higher education institutions. This study examines academic records from the Information and Communication Technologies Engineering program at the Instituto Tecnológico de Tlalnepantla for the 2021–2023 period to identify trends in approval, failure, and dropout rates. A mixed-methods approach with a convergent design and a descriptive-analytical scope was adopted. The quantitative phase involved the analysis of approximately 2,475 institutional academic records covering 15 courses offered over six academic semesters, while the qualitative phase incorporated questionnaires and semi structured interviews to enrich the interpretation of the findings. The results revealed a progressive increase in course approval rates and a decline in student dropout. In addition, programming, mathematics, databases, and communication systems were identified as the subjects with the highest academic difficulty. These findings provide evidence to support institutional decision-making aimed at strengthening tutoring programs, academic monitoring, and student retention strategies in engineering education.

title: Determinant factors in the teaching-learning process of software development: An AI-Assisted analysis
abstract: The objective of this study is to determine which factors influence the teaching and learning process of programming related subjects. Methodologically, a data collection instrument was applied using a purposive non-probability sampling technique to a sample of 39 students in a face-to-face and online learning environment. Data processing was performed using artificial intelligence tools. The results reveal that 85% of the subjects show positive aptitudes driven by vocation and a cognitive exhaustion index of 72%. This finding highlights that mental overload makes vocational interest insufficient, since abstract thinking is necessary for the coding process. The contribution of this work is to offer a diagnostic tool for the creation of pedagogical strategies that improve academic performance by mitigating mental exhaustion without affecting student motivation.

title: Education 5.0 and cognitive inclusion: Cyber-Physical Perspectives on Neurodiversity in Higher Education
abstract: This study analyzes the epistemic transition toward Education 5.0 in higher education, exploring the convergence between cyber-physical environments and neurodiversity. The general objective is to descriptively evaluate university students' perceptions regarding cognitive inclusion and disruptive technologies in the contemporary foreign language classroom. Methodologically, quantitative cross-sectional empirical research was developed through a simple random sampling in a single assessment session. The sample comprised 188 International Business undergraduate students from the Universidad Autónoma de Nayarit, enrolled in morning and evening shifts across all curricular semesters; sociodemographically, 71% corresponded to women and 29% to men. The data collection technique was a survey, administered via Google Forms, utilizing a structured Likert scale instrument composed of seven items, each configured with four response options. The results demonstrate a marked receptivity toward adaptive algorithmic tools as personalized learning environments. It is concluded that the 5.0 model promotes ethical governance and intellectual emancipation, transforming cognitive plurality into a strategic human advantage against global technical standardization within public academic institutions.

title: Generative artificial intelligence and the development of English oral skills: perceptions of pre-service English language teachers
abstract: This study explored the perceptions of future English teachers regarding the use of generative artificial intelligence [GAI], using ChatGPT and Gemini Flash as tools to support the development of oral English skills. The objective was to document and analyze the students’ experiences with an interaction that incorporated guided conversations, role-playing, and pronunciation training. An exploratory-descriptive qualitative approach was adopted, involving 21 B1-level students from the Escuela Normal de Atlacomulco, of whom 8 were selected for semistructured interviews. The results revealed benefits such as immediate and personalized feedback and increased speaking practice outside the classroom, along with limitations related to connectivity and unequal access to devices. The main contribution lies in providing empirical evidence on the potential and limitations of GAI for academic purposes.

title: From the discovery of the neutron to Machine Learning: The scientific and technological evolution of nuclear engineering
abstract: Nuclear engineering has evolved for more than a century through scientific discoveries that progressively transformed the understanding of atomic structure and the utilization of nuclear energy. The objective of this article is to present a historical and scientific perspective on the evolution of nuclear engineering, from the discovery of X-rays and radioactivity to the development of computational methods based on reactor physics, Monte Carlo simulations, and artificial intelligence. The methodology consisted of a documentary review of seminal scientific publications and recent specialized literature, analyzed chronologically to relate major scientific milestones with the evolution of computational tools. The review describes the transition from deterministic methods and Monte Carlo simulations to Machine Learning, Physics-Informed Neural Networks, Digital Twins, and Explainable Artificial Intelligence, highlighting that these technologies complement traditional physics-based models rather than replacing them. This review integrates historical, scientific, technological, and computational advances into a coherent narrative of modern nuclear engineering evolution.

title: Risk Based Strategic Alignment in Higher Education: Governance, Digital Transformation, and Sustainability Outcomes
abstract: Higher education institutions increasingly operate in digital environments that require stronger integration among governance, risk management, digital transformation, and sustainability outcomes. However, the literature on strategic risk, digital governance, artificial intelligence adoption, cybersecurity, learning analytics, and institutional sustainability in higher education remains dispersed across different research streams. This article aims to synthesize the literature on risk-based strategic alignment as a mechanism linking governance, digital transformation, and sustainability outcomes in higher education. The study employed a systematic literature review using the PCC framework and a narrative-integrative thematic synthesis approach. The Scopus search identified 96 records. After database filtering, 62 records were excluded, 34 reports were sought for retrieval, 14 reports were not retrieved, 20 reports were assessed for eligibility, and 10 studies were included in the main synthesis. The findings reveal five major patterns: strategic risk in higher education is multidimensional; governance mechanisms serve as the main instruments for risk-based alignment; digital transformation functions both as an institutional enabler and as a source of risk; sustainability outcomes are more frequently represented through resilience, responsible artificial intelligence, educational equity, and sustainable digital education than through direct sustainability performance indicators; and no dominant theoretical model has yet consolidated the relationship among these domains. The study concludes that risk-based strategic alignment offers an integrative lens for understanding how higher education institutions connect risk visibility, governance capacity, digital transformation, and sustainability-oriented outcomes.

title: The trajectory of educational justice in Zimbabwe's post-independence education policies and reforms (1980-2026): Implications for future educational reforms
abstract: Purpose This study examines the evolution of Zimbabwe’s post-independence education policies through the lens of educational justice. Drawing on Rawls’ theories of distributive justice and equality of opportunity, and Fraser’s theories of recognition and participatory parity, the study explains how conceptions of educational justice and corresponding policy priorities evolved over time. Methodology Situated within interpretive and transformative research paradigms, the study employs historical research and interpretive policy analysis to examine major national education policies enacted from 1980 to 2026. Policies and reforms were purposively selected based on their significance to educational justice. These include universal education reforms, the Basic Education Assistance Module, Early Childhood Development initiative, language-in-education reforms, the Inclusive Education policy, and the Policy on the Re-entry of Pregnant Learners. Policy documents were analyzed using deductive coding guided by four analytical domains: redistribution, equality of opportunity, recognition, and participation. The Capability Approach subsequently informed the interpretation of the developmental trajectory by assessing the extent to which successive reforms expanded learners’ capabilities to achieve valued educational outcomes. Findings The findings reveal that Zimbabwe’s post-independence education policies reflect a progressive broadening of educational justice. Early reforms primarily addressed colonial inequalities through the redistributive expansion of educational access. Subsequent policies increasingly targeted socioeconomic disadvantage, promoted fair equality of opportunity, recognized learner diversity, and strengthened conditions for meaningful participation. Collectively, the reforms demonstrate a cumulative developmental trajectory in which educational justice evolved from a predominantly distributive concern toward a multidimensional policy discourse. Although the developmental trajectory represents important normative progress, interpretation through the Capability Approach suggests that persistent structural and contextual constraints continue to limit learners’ ability to translate educational opportunities into valued life outcomes. Significance This study contributes to education policy scholarship by introducing the Developmental Trajectory of Educational Justice as a conceptual framework for explaining how educational justice evolves across successive policy reforms. Beyond its theoretical contribution, the framework offers practical guidance for policymakers by demonstrating that educational justice is a dynamic concept requiring continual adaptation as new forms of educational disadvantage emerge. As educational systems respond to new challenges such as curriculum reform, digital inequalities, and the growing integration of artificial intelligence, the framework can inform the design of future educational reforms that anticipate and address emerging injustices.

title: A Bibliometric Systematic Review of Blockchain Integration in E-commerce with Emphasis on Data Privacy and Supply Chain Transparency
abstract: Driven by digital transformation and evolving consumer behavior, the e-commerce industry continues to grow rapidly across global markets. Blockchain, as an emerging technology, offers transformative potential for e-commerce operations due to its transparency, security, decentralization, and traceability features. These attributes enable improvements in areas such as data privacy, supply chain traceability, fraud prevention, and operational efficiency. However, the adoption and integration of blockchain in e-commerce remain in a nascent stage, with significant technological and regulatory hurdles yet to be overcome. This paper conducts a systematic review of blockchain applications in e-commerce with emphasis on data privacy and supply chain transparency by utilizing bibliometric techniques. All relevant publications indexed in the Scopus database were examined to extract and analyze keywords and themes. Additionally, VOSviewer software was employed to visualize co-authorship, keyword co-occurrence, and thematic clusters. Findings reveal that blockchain contributes to various domains within e-commerce, including data security, supply chain transparency, sector-specific applications, and integration with emerging technologies such as AI and IoT. Key drivers for blockchain adoption include improved traceability, automation, and fraud prevention, while barriers such as scalability, regulatory uncertainty, and high implementation costs continue to hinder widespread integration. The study offers valuable implications for both academic researchers and industry practitioners seeking to adopt blockchain for enhancing e-commerce performance.

title: IMPLIKASI PENGGUNAAN KECERDASAN BUATAN DALAM MEDIA SOSIAL TERHADAP PEMBINAAN AKHLAK MASYARAKAT: ANALISIS USUL FIQH BERASASKAN SADD AL-DHARA’I DAN I‘TIBAR AL-MA’ALAT
abstract: Kajian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis implikasi penggunaan Kecerdasan Buatan (Artificial Intelligence, AI) dalam media sosial terhadap pembinaan akhlak masyarakat berdasarkan perspektif usul fiqh, khususnya prinsip Sadd al-Dhara’i. Perkembangan pesat AI dalam era digital telah mengubah cara manusia berkomunikasi dan berinteraksi, namun pada masa yang sama turut membawa cabaran terhadap nilai dan etika dalam masyarakat. Kajian ini menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif melalui kaedah analisis kandungan terhadap pelbagai sumber sekunder seperti artikel jurnal, laporan serta karya ulama dalam bidang usul fiqh. Hasil kajian menunjukkan bahawa penggunaan AI dalam media sosial menyumbang kepada peningkatan penyebaran maklumat palsu, penipuan dalam talian serta pembentukan tingkah laku tidak beretika akibat pengaruh algoritma dan pendedahan berulang kepada kandungan tertentu. Berdasarkan prinsip Sadd al-Dhara’i yang diperkukuhkan dengan konsep i`tibar al-ma`alat, penggunaan AI yang berpotensi membawa kepada kemudaratan perlu dikawal bagi mengelakkan kerosakan akhlak yang lebih besar dalam masyarakat. Sehubungan itu, kajian ini mencadangkan pendekatan yang lebih proaktif dan bersifat pencegahan melalui pengukuhan dasar, peningkatan literasi digital serta penglibatan aktif institusi sosial dalam membimbing masyarakat menggunakan teknologi secara beretika. Justeru, kajian ini menyumbang kepada pengembangan aplikasi prinsip usul fiqh dalam menilai isu teknologi semasa serta menekankan kepentingan mengekalkan keseimbangan antara kemajuan teknologi dan pembinaan akhlak masyarakat.

title: Digital Rupee Adoption: Blockchain’s Role in India’s Central Bank Digital Currency
abstract: India's Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC), the digital rupee (e₹), was introduced to support the transformation of the country's digital payment and financial ecosystem; however, its adoption remains relatively limited. This study examines the factors influencing technology valuation and adoption intention toward e₹ in India. Specifically, the study investigates the effects of competition from other payment options, digital illiteracy, financial inclusion, economic growth, payment diversity, scalability, and secure and centralized systems on technology valuation, and further examines the effect of technology valuation on adoption intention. Data were collected from 252 respondents using a fully structured questionnaire, representing a 63% response rate. The proposed model was empirically assessed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The findings indicate that competition from other payment options, digital illiteracy, financial inclusion, economic growth, payment diversity, and secure and centralized systems have statistically significant positive effects on technology valuation. In contrast, scalability has a positive but statistically non-significant relationship with technology valuation. Technology valuation has a strong and statistically significant positive effect on adoption intention (β = 0.794, p < 0.001). The structural model explains 89.1% of the variance in technology valuation and 63.1% of the variance in adoption intention. Overall, the findings demonstrate that the adoption of e₹ is influenced by a combination of economic, financial, competitive, payment-related, and technological considerations. The study contributes to the emerging literature on CBDC adoption by highlighting the importance of technology valuation as a key mechanism through which characteristics of the digital-currency ecosystem influence users' intention to adopt e₹.

title: Automated Performance Evaluation and Due Process in Disciplinary Procedures
abstract: Digital technologies that are now increasingly being adopted in HRM have changed the way in which performance of employees is measured, monitored, evaluated, and managed. The systems for Automated Performance Evaluation (APE) make use of such technologies as rule-based scoring, key performance indicators (KPIs), machine learning, employee monitoring software, natural language processing (NLP), and Human Resource Information Systems (HRIS) for evaluating the behavior and performance of employees. While there is an array of advantages that the implementation of these technologies may bring, there are significant issues associated with the use of these technologies for disciplining. The score that is assigned by algorithms may have a bearing on any warning issued to the employee, development of performance improvement plan, suspension, promotion, termination, or any other decision affecting the employment. The study seeks to explore the link between automated performance evaluation and due process in workplace discipline proceedings. Concepts such as APE, algorithmic management, natural justice, and organizational justice will be developed. The study shall also explore technologies used in automatic evaluation of employee performances and how such technologies could be used in various phases of discipline processes. Special consideration shall be given to the right to notice, being given a chance to hear oneself, access to information/evidence, impartiality of decisions, explanations of algorithmic decisions, and the possibility of human review. Legal considerations include Indian labour laws and employment law principles, the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and the Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 as well as the international approaches such as the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), EU Artificial Intelligence Act among others. The paper discusses some of the challenges associated with automated evaluation of employee performance such as opacity of algorithms, discrimination or bias, inaccuracies in the use of data, failure to take context into consideration, over monitoring, accountability issues, and power asymmetry. Finally, an automated evaluation process that is consistent with due process is developed.

title: Adaptive learning via digital platforms for the personalization of foreign language learning
abstract: Nowadays, tailoring instruction to the individual student through digital resources is no longer a novelty, particularly in English as a Foreign Language [EFL] classes. It is common to find platforms that adjust difficulty levels based on user interactions. To understand how this works in practice, 96 university students were monitored over 16weeks, using questionnaires and interviews for data collection. The results showed a favorable reception of the tools used, largely because they enabled students to progress at their own pace, receive instant feedback, become more independent in their studies, and maintain high levels of motivation. However, the students noted that teacher guidance remains essential throughout the instructional process, as technology serves merely as a complement.

title: The Homo Sapiens digitalis in society 5.0 towards a sustainable and ethical entrepreneurship
abstract: The article The Homo Sapiens Digitalis in Society 5.0 Towards a Sustainable and Ethical Entrepreneurship explores the evolution of cognitive and technological identity in Mexican higher education, focusing on the development of business models with a profound humanistic vision. The main objective of the research was to analyze the perceptions of 98 undergraduate students in International Business at the Universidad Autónoma de Nayarit, from both morning and afternoon shifts, regarding the viability of entrepreneurship that links smart city innovation with a democratic framework. In this context, the data collection technique consisted of administering a Google Forms questionnaire structured under a Likert scale with seven key items and four response options. The participants, whose sample comprised 57 percent women and 43 percent men from different semesters, were consulted about the ethical challenges of the infosphere, the urgency of urban sustainability, the impact of artificial intelligence, and the psychosocial risks associated with self-entrepreneurship. The results reflect a high sensitivity toward social responsibility, suggesting that higher education must lead the transition toward Society 5.0 through pedagogical strategies that transcend technological determinism and strengthen collective socioemotional intelligence.

title: AI-DIGITAL HUMAN AS A NEW CLASS OF DIGITAL LAW SUBJECT: TYPOLOGY, CRITERIA OF LEGAL PERSONHOOD, AND A REGISTRATION MODEL IN DIGITAL ECOSYSTEMS
abstract: This article argues for a new class of digital legal subject within AI legal-personhood doctrine — the ‘AI-digital human’ — largely unaddressed in domestic and international legal scholarship. Building on the author’s earlier three-class model of AI legal subjects and the institution of the AI-representative, the article distinguishes two different modules of the AI-digital human: Module 1 (Digiperson), a digital human as a functional reflection of a specific natural person, built on ‘red-group’ identification attributes and digitised access credentials; and Module 2 (autonomous Digihuman), reflecting no real natural person, its attributes formed referentially and tied to a functional role within a digital ecosystem. The article shows that equating a digital human with a natural person in the full scope of rights and obligations is a doctrinal error: legal status should follow an age-based logic (child—adolescent—adult) rather than mirroring the prototype’s status. Drawing on a comparative analysis of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (AI Act) and Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (eIDAS 2.0), the article substantiates the need for a Digital Humans Registry as an institutional legitimation mechanism for both modules, and formulates draft articles for the Ukrainian Law on Artificial Intelligence.
